lines.text: Make boot upon the summer’s velvet buds,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Which pillage they with merry march bring home

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: To the tent-royal of their emperor;

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Who, busied in his majesty, surveys

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: The singing masons building roofs of gold,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: The civil citizens kneading up the honey,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: The poor mechanic porters crowding in

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Their heavy burdens at his narrow gate,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: The sad-eyed justice, with his surly hum,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Delivering o’er to executors pale

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: The lazy yawning drone. I this infer,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: That many things, having full reference

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: To one consent, may work contrariously.

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: As many arrows, loosed several ways,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Come to one mark; as many ways meet in one town;

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: As many fresh streams meet in one salt sea;

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: As many lines close in the dial’s centre;

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: So many a thousand actions, once afoot,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: End in one purpose, and be all well borne

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Without defeat. Therefore to France, my liege!

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Divide your happy England into four,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Whereof take you one quarter into France,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: And you withal shall make all Gallia shake.

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: If we, with thrice such powers left at home,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Cannot defend our own doors from the dog,

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: Let us be worried and our nation lose

lines.speaker: CANTERBURY
lines.text: The name of hardiness and policy.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Call in the messengers sent from the Dauphin.
[_Exeunt some Attendants._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now are we well resolv’d; and, by God’s help,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And yours, the noble sinews of our power,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: France being ours, we’ll bend it to our awe,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or break it all to pieces. Or there we’ll sit,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ruling in large and ample empery

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O’er France and all her almost kingly dukedoms,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or lay these bones in an unworthy urn,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tombless, with no remembrance over them.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Either our history shall with full mouth

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Speak freely of our acts, or else our grave,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Like Turkish mute, shall have a tongueless mouth,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not worshipp’d with a waxen epitaph.
Enter Ambassadors of France.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now are we well prepar’d to know the pleasure

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of our fair cousin Dauphin; for we hear

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your greeting is from him, not from the King.

lines.speaker: FIRST AMBASSADOR
lines.text: May’t please your Majesty to give us leave

lines.speaker: FIRST AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Freely to render what we have in charge,

lines.speaker: FIRST AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Or shall we sparingly show you far off

lines.speaker: FIRST AMBASSADOR
lines.text: The Dauphin’s meaning and our embassy?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We are no tyrant, but a Christian king,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Unto whose grace our passion is as subject

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As is our wretches fett’red in our prisons;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore with frank and with uncurbed plainness

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tell us the Dauphin’s mind.

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Thus, then, in few.

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Your Highness, lately sending into France,

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Did claim some certain dukedoms, in the right

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Of your great predecessor, King Edward the Third.

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: In answer of which claim, the prince our master

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Says that you savour too much of your youth,

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: And bids you be advis’d there’s nought in France

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: That can be with a nimble galliard won.

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: You cannot revel into dukedoms there.

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: He therefore sends you, meeter for your spirit,

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: This tun of treasure; and, in lieu of this,

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Desires you let the dukedoms that you claim

lines.speaker: AMBASSADOR
lines.text: Hear no more of you. This the Dauphin speaks.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What treasure, uncle?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Tennis-balls, my liege.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We are glad the Dauphin is so pleasant with us.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His present and your pains we thank you for.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When we have match’d our rackets to these balls,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We will, in France, by God’s grace, play a set

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall strike his father’s crown into the hazard.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tell him he hath made a match with such a wrangler

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That all the courts of France will be disturb’d

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With chaces. And we understand him well,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How he comes o’er us with our wilder days,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not measuring what use we made of them.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We never valu’d this poor seat of England;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And therefore, living hence, did give ourself

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To barbarous licence; as ’tis ever common

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That men are merriest when they are from home.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But tell the Dauphin I will keep my state,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be like a king, and show my sail of greatness

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When I do rouse me in my throne of France.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For that I have laid by my majesty

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And plodded like a man for working days,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But I will rise there with so full a glory

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That I will dazzle all the eyes of France,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yea, strike the Dauphin blind to look on us.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And tell the pleasant prince this mock of his

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hath turn’d his balls to gun-stones, and his soul

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall stand sore charged for the wasteful vengeance

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That shall fly with them; for many a thousand widows

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall this his mock mock out of their dear husbands,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Mock mothers from their sons, mock castles down;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And some are yet ungotten and unborn

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That shall have cause to curse the Dauphin’s scorn.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But this lies all within the will of God,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To whom I do appeal; and in whose name

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tell you the Dauphin I am coming on

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To venge me as I may, and to put forth

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My rightful hand in a well-hallow’d cause.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So get you hence in peace; and tell the Dauphin

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: His jest will savour but of shallow wit,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When thousands weep more than did laugh at it.—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Convey them with safe conduct.—Fare you well.
[_Exeunt Ambassadors._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: This was a merry message.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We hope to make the sender blush at it.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore, my lords, omit no happy hour

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That may give furtherance to our expedition;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For we have now no thought in us but France,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Save those to God, that run before our business.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore, let our proportions for these wars

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be soon collected, and all things thought upon

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That may with reasonable swiftness add

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: More feathers to our wings; for, God before,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We’ll chide this Dauphin at his father’s door.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore let every man now task his thought,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That this fair action may on foot be brought.
[_Exeunt._]
Flourish. Enter Chorus.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Now all the youth of England are on fire,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And silken dalliance in the wardrobe lies.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Now thrive the armourers, and honour’s thought

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Reigns solely in the breast of every man.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: They sell the pasture now to buy the horse,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Following the mirror of all Christian kings,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With winged heels, as English Mercuries.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: For now sits Expectation in the air,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And hides a sword from hilts unto the point

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With crowns imperial, crowns, and coronets,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Promis’d to Harry and his followers.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The French, advis’d by good intelligence

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Of this most dreadful preparation,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Shake in their fear, and with pale policy

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Seek to divert the English purposes.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: O England! model to thy inward greatness,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Like little body with a mighty heart,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: What mightst thou do, that honour would thee do,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Were all thy children kind and natural!

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: But see thy fault! France hath in thee found out

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: A nest of hollow bosoms, which he fills

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With treacherous crowns; and three corrupted men,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: One, Richard Earl of Cambridge, and the second,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Henry Lord Scroop of Masham, and the third,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Sir Thomas Grey, knight of Northumberland,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Have, for the gilt of France,—O guilt indeed!—

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Confirm’d conspiracy with fearful France;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And by their hands this grace of kings must die,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: If hell and treason hold their promises,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Ere he take ship for France, and in Southampton.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Linger your patience on, and we’ll digest

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The abuse of distance, force a play.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The sum is paid; the traitors are agreed;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The King is set from London; and the scene

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Is now transported, gentles, to Southampton.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: There is the playhouse now, there must you sit;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And thence to France shall we convey you safe,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And bring you back, charming the narrow seas

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: To give you gentle pass; for, if we may,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: We’ll not offend one stomach with our play.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: But, till the King come forth, and not till then,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Unto Southampton do we shift our scene.
[_Exit._]
Enter Corporal Nym and Lieutenant Bardolph.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Well met, Corporal Nym.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Good morrow, Lieutenant Bardolph.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: What, are Ancient Pistol and you friends yet?

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: For my part, I care not. I say little; but when time shall serve, there

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: shall be smiles; but that shall be as it may. I dare not fight, but I

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: will wink and hold out mine iron. It is a simple one, but what though?

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: It will toast cheese, and it will endure cold as another man’s sword

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: will; and there’s an end.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: I will bestow a breakfast to make you friends; and we’ll be all three

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: sworn brothers to France. Let it be so, good Corporal Nym.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Faith, I will live so long as I may, that’s the certain of it; and when

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I cannot live any longer, I will do as I may. That is my rest, that is

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: the rendezvous of it.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: It is certain, corporal, that he is married to Nell Quickly; and

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: certainly she did you wrong, for you were troth-plight to her.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I cannot tell. Things must be as they may. Men may sleep, and they may

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: have their throats about them at that time; and some say knives have

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: edges. It must be as it may. Though patience be a tired mare, yet she

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: will plod. There must be conclusions. Well, I cannot tell.
Enter Pistol and Hostess.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Here comes Ancient Pistol and his wife. Good Corporal, be patient here.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: How now, mine host Pistol!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Base tike, call’st thou me host?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Now, by this hand, I swear I scorn the term;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Nor shall my Nell keep lodgers.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: No, by my troth, not long; for we cannot lodge and board a dozen or

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: fourteen gentlewomen that live honestly by the prick of their needles,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: but it will be thought we keep a bawdy house straight. [_Nym and Pistol

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: draw._] O well a day, Lady, if he be not drawn now! We shall see wilful

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: adultery and murder committed.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Good Lieutenant! good corporal! offer nothing here.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Pish!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Pish for thee, Iceland dog! thou prick-ear’d cur of Iceland!

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Good Corporal Nym, show thy valour, and put up your sword.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Will you shog off? I would have you _solus_.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: _Solus_, egregious dog! O viper vile!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The _solus_ in thy most mervailous face;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The _solus_ in thy teeth, and in thy throat,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And in thy hateful lungs, yea, in thy maw, perdy,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And, which is worse, within thy nasty mouth!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I do retort the _solus_ in thy bowels;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: For I can take, and Pistol’s cock is up,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And flashing fire will follow.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I am not Barbason; you cannot conjure me. I have an humour to knock you

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: indifferently well. If you grow foul with me, Pistol, I will scour you

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: with my rapier, as I may, in fair terms. If you would walk off, I would

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: prick your guts a little, in good terms, as I may; and that’s the

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: humour of it.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: O braggart vile and damned furious wight!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The grave doth gape, and doting death is near,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Therefore exhale.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Hear me, hear me what I say. He that strikes the first stroke I’ll run

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: him up to the hilts, as I am a soldier.
[_Draws._]

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: An oath of mickle might; and fury shall abate.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Give me thy fist, thy fore-foot to me give.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Thy spirits are most tall.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I will cut thy throat, one time or other, in fair terms: that is the

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: humour of it.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: “Couple a gorge!”

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: That is the word. I thee defy again.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: O hound of Crete, think’st thou my spouse to get?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: No! to the spital go,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And from the powdering tub of infamy

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Fetch forth the lazar kite of Cressid’s kind,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Doll Tearsheet she by name, and her espouse.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I have, and I will hold, the quondam Quickly

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: For the only she; and _pauca_, there’s enough.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Go to.
Enter the Boy.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Mine host Pistol, you must come to my master, and you, hostess. He is

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: very sick, and would to bed. Good Bardolph, put thy face between his

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: sheets, and do the office of a warming-pan. Faith, he’s very ill.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Away, you rogue!

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: By my troth, he’ll yield the crow a pudding one of these days.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: The King has kill’d his heart.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Good husband, come home presently.
[_Exeunt Hostess and Boy._]

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Come, shall I make you two friends? We must to France together; why the

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: devil should we keep knives to cut one another’s throats?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Let floods o’erswell, and fiends for food howl on!

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: You’ll pay me the eight shillings I won of you at betting?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Base is the slave that pays.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: That now I will have: that’s the humour of it.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: As manhood shall compound. Push home.
[_They draw._]

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: By this sword, he that makes the first thrust, I’ll kill him; by this

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: sword, I will.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Sword is an oath, and oaths must have their course.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Corporal Nym, and thou wilt be friends, be friends; an thou wilt not,

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: why, then, be enemies with me too. Prithee, put up.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I shall have my eight shillings I won from you at betting?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: A noble shalt thou have, and present pay;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And liquor likewise will I give to thee,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And friendship shall combine, and brotherhood.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I’ll live by Nym, and Nym shall live by me.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Is not this just? For I shall sutler be

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Unto the camp, and profits will accrue.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Give me thy hand.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I shall have my noble?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: In cash most justly paid.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Well, then, that’s the humour of’t.
Enter Hostess.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: As ever you come of women, come in quickly to Sir John.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Ah, poor heart! he is so shak’d of a burning quotidian tertian,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: that it is most lamentable to behold. Sweet men, come to him.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: The King hath run bad humours on the knight; that’s the even of it.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Nym, thou hast spoke the right.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: His heart is fracted and corroborate.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: The King is a good king; but it must be as it may; he passes some

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: humours and careers.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Let us condole the knight; for, lambkins, we will live.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Exeter, Bedford and Westmorland.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: ’Fore God, his Grace is bold, to trust these traitors.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: They shall be apprehended by and by.

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: How smooth and even they do bear themselves!

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: As if allegiance in their bosoms sat

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: Crowned with faith and constant loyalty.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: The King hath note of all that they intend,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: By interception which they dream not of.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Nay, but the man that was his bed-fellow,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Whom he hath dull’d and cloy’d with gracious favours,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That he should, for a foreign purse, so sell

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: His sovereign’s life to death and treachery.
Trumpets sound. Enter King Henry, Scroop, Cambridge and Grey.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now sits the wind fair, and we will aboard.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My Lord of Cambridge, and my kind Lord of Masham,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And you, my gentle knight, give me your thoughts.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Up in the air, crown’d with the golden sun,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Saw his heroical seed, and smil’d to see him,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Mangle the work of nature and deface

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: The patterns that by God and by French fathers

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Had twenty years been made. This is a stem

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Of that victorious stock; and let us fear

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: The native mightiness and fate of him.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Ambassadors from Harry King of England

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Do crave admittance to your Majesty.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: We’ll give them present audience. Go, and bring them.
[_Exeunt Messenger and certain Lords._]

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: You see this chase is hotly follow’d, friends.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Turn head and stop pursuit; for coward dogs

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Most spend their mouths when what they seem to threaten

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Runs far before them. Good my sovereign,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Take up the English short, and let them know

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Of what a monarchy you are the head.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Self-love, my liege, is not so vile a sin

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: As self-neglecting.
Enter Exeter.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: From our brother of England?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: From him; and thus he greets your Majesty:

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He wills you, in the name of God Almighty,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That you divest yourself, and lay apart

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The borrowed glories that by gift of heaven,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: By law of nature and of nations, ’longs

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: To him and to his heirs; namely, the crown

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And all wide-stretched honours that pertain

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: By custom and the ordinance of times

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Unto the crown of France. That you may know

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: ’Tis no sinister nor no awkward claim

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Pick’d from the worm-holes of long-vanish’d days,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Nor from the dust of old oblivion rak’d,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He sends you this most memorable line,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: In every branch truly demonstrative;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Willing you overlook this pedigree;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And when you find him evenly deriv’d

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: From his most fam’d of famous ancestors,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Edward the Third, he bids you then resign

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Your crown and kingdom, indirectly held

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: From him, the native and true challenger.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Or else what follows?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Bloody constraint; for if you hide the crown

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Even in your hearts, there will he rake for it.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Therefore in fierce tempest is he coming,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: In thunder and in earthquake, like a Jove,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That, if requiring fail, he will compel;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And bids you, in the bowels of the Lord,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Deliver up the crown, and to take mercy

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: On the poor souls for whom this hungry war

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Opens his vasty jaws; and on your head

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Turning the widows’ tears, the orphans’ cries,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The dead men’s blood, the pining maidens’ groans,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: For husbands, fathers, and betrothed lovers,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That shall be swallowed in this controversy.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: This is his claim, his threat’ning, and my message;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Unless the Dauphin be in presence here,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: To whom expressly I bring greeting too.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: For us, we will consider of this further.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Tomorrow shall you bear our full intent

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Back to our brother of England.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: For the Dauphin,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: I stand here for him. What to him from England?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Scorn and defiance. Slight regard, contempt,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And anything that may not misbecome

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The mighty sender, doth he prize you at.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Thus says my king: an if your father’s Highness

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Do not, in grant of all demands at large,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Sweeten the bitter mock you sent his Majesty,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He’ll call you to so hot an answer of it

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That caves and womby vaultages of France

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Shall chide your trespass and return your mock

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: In second accent of his ordinance.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Say, if my father render fair return,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: It is against my will; for I desire

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Nothing but odds with England. To that end,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: As matching to his youth and vanity,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: I did present him with the Paris balls.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He’ll make your Paris Louvre shake for it,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Were it the mistress-court of mighty Europe;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And, be assur’d, you’ll find a difference,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: As we his subjects have in wonder found,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Between the promise of his greener days

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And these he masters now. Now he weighs time

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Even to the utmost grain. That you shall read

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: In your own losses, if he stay in France.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Tomorrow shall you know our mind at full.
[_Flourish._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Dispatch us with all speed, lest that our king

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Come here himself to question our delay;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: For he is footed in this land already.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: You shall be soon dispatch’d with fair conditions.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: A night is but small breath and little pause

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: To answer matters of this consequence.
[_Exeunt._]
Flourish. Enter Chorus.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Thus with imagin’d wing our swift scene flies,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: In motion of no less celerity

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Than that of thought. Suppose that you have seen

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The well-appointed king at Hampton pier

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Embark his royalty, and his brave fleet

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With silken streamers the young Phoebus fanning.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Play with your fancies; and in them behold

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Upon the hempen tackle ship-boys climbing;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Hear the shrill whistle which doth order give

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: To sounds confus’d; behold the threaden sails,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Borne with the invisible and creeping wind,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Draw the huge bottoms through the furrow’d sea,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Breasting the lofty surge. O, do but think

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: You stand upon the rivage and behold

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: A city on the inconstant billows dancing;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: For so appears this fleet majestical,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Holding due course to Harfleur. Follow, follow!

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Grapple your minds to sternage of this navy,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And leave your England, as dead midnight still,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Guarded with grandsires, babies, and old women,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Either past or not arriv’d to pith and puissance.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: For who is he, whose chin is but enrich’d

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With one appearing hair, that will not follow

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: These cull’d and choice-drawn cavaliers to France?

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Work, work your thoughts, and therein see a siege;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Behold the ordnance on their carriages,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With fatal mouths gaping on girded Harfleur.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Suppose the ambassador from the French comes back,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Tells Harry that the King doth offer him

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Katharine his daughter, and with her, to dowry,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Some petty and unprofitable dukedoms.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The offer likes not; and the nimble gunner

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With linstock now the devilish cannon touches,
[_Alarum, and chambers go off._]

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And down goes all before them. Still be kind,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And eke out our performance with your mind.
[_Exit._]
Alarum. Enter King Henry, Exeter, Bedford, Gloucester and Soldiers, with scaling-ladders.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or close the wall up with our English dead.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In peace there’s nothing so becomes a man

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As modest stillness and humility;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But when the blast of war blows in our ears,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then imitate the action of the tiger;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stiffen the sinews, summon up the blood,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Disguise fair nature with hard-favour’d rage;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then lend the eye a terrible aspect;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let it pry through the portage of the head

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Like the brass cannon; let the brow o’erwhelm it

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As fearfully as does a galled rock

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O’erhang and jutty his confounded base,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Swill’d with the wild and wasteful ocean.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now set the teeth and stretch the nostril wide,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hold hard the breath, and bend up every spirit

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To his full height. On, on, you noblest English,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose blood is fet from fathers of war-proof!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Fathers that, like so many Alexanders,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Have in these parts from morn till even fought,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And sheath’d their swords for lack of argument.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Dishonour not your mothers; now attest

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That those whom you call’d fathers did beget you.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be copy now to men of grosser blood,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And teach them how to war. And you, good yeomen,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose limbs were made in England, show us here

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The mettle of your pasture; let us swear

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That you are worth your breeding, which I doubt not;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For there is none of you so mean and base,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That hath not noble lustre in your eyes.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I see you stand like greyhounds in the slips,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Straining upon the start. The game’s afoot!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Follow your spirit, and upon this charge

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Cry, “God for Harry! England and Saint George!”
[_Exeunt. Alarum, and chambers go off._]
Enter Nym, Bardolph, Pistol and Boy.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: On, on, on, on, on! To the breach, to the breach!

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Pray thee, corporal, stay. The knocks are too hot; and, for mine own

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: part, I have not a case of lives. The humour of it is too hot; that is

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: the very plain-song of it.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The plain-song is most just, for humours do abound.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Knocks go and come; God’s vassals drop and die;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And sword and shield,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: In bloody field,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Doth win immortal fame.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Would I were in an alehouse in London! I would give all my fame for a

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: pot of ale and safety.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And I.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: If wishes would prevail with me,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: My purpose should not fail with me,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: But thither would I hie.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: As duly,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: But not as truly,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: As bird doth sing on bough.
Enter Fluellen.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Up to the breach, you dogs! Avaunt, you cullions!
[_Driving them forward._]

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Be merciful, great Duke, to men of mould.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Abate thy rage, abate thy manly rage,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Abate thy rage, great Duke!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Good bawcock, bate thy rage; use lenity, sweet chuck!

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: These be good humours! Your honour wins bad humours.
[_Exeunt all but Boy._]

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: As young as I am, I have observ’d these three swashers. I am boy to

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: them all three; but all they three, though they would serve me, could

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: not be man to me; for indeed three such antics do not amount to a man.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: For Bardolph, he is white-liver’d and red-fac’d; by the means whereof

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: ’a faces it out, but fights not. For Pistol, he hath a killing tongue

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: and a quiet sword; by the means whereof ’a breaks words, and keeps

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: whole weapons. For Nym, he hath heard that men of few words are the

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: best men; and therefore he scorns to say his prayers, lest ’a should be

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: thought a coward. But his few bad words are match’d with as few good

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: deeds; for ’a never broke any man’s head but his own, and that was

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: against a post when he was drunk. They will steal anything, and call it

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: purchase. Bardolph stole a lute-case, bore it twelve leagues, and sold

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: it for three half-pence. Nym and Bardolph are sworn brothers in

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: filching, and in Calais they stole a fire-shovel. I knew by that piece

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: of service the men would carry coals. They would have me as familiar

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: with men’s pockets as their gloves or their handkerchers; which makes

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: much against my manhood, if I should take from another’s pocket to put

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: into mine; for it is plain pocketing up of wrongs. I must leave them,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: and seek some better service. Their villainy goes against my weak

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: stomach, and therefore I must cast it up.
[_Exit._]
Enter Gower and Fluellen.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Captain Fluellen, you must come presently to the mines.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: The Duke of Gloucester would speak with you.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: To the mines! Tell you the Duke, it is not so good to come to the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: mines; for, look you, the mines is not according to the disciplines of

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: the war. The concavities of it is not sufficient; for, look you, the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: athversary, you may discuss unto the Duke, look you, is digt himself

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: four yard under the countermines. By Cheshu, I think ’a will plow up

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: all, if there is not better directions.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: The Duke of Gloucester, to whom the order of the siege is given, is

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: altogether directed by an Irishman, a very valiant gentleman, i’ faith.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: It is Captain Macmorris, is it not?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: I think it be.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: By Cheshu, he is an ass, as in the world. I will verify as much in his

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: beard. He has no more directions in the true disciplines of the wars,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: look you, of the Roman disciplines, than is a puppy-dog.
Enter Macmorris and Captain Jamy.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Here ’a comes; and the Scots captain, Captain Jamy, with him.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Captain Jamy is a marvellous falorous gentleman, that is certain; and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: of great expedition and knowledge in the anchient wars, upon my

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: particular knowledge of his directions. By Cheshu, he will maintain his

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: argument as well as any military man in the world, in the disciplines

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: of the pristine wars of the Romans.

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: I say gud-day, Captain Fluellen.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: God-den to your worship, good Captain James.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: How now, Captain Macmorris! have you quit the mines?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Have the pioneers given o’er?

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: By Chrish, la! ’tish ill done! The work ish give over, the trompet

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: sound the retreat. By my hand I swear, and my father’s soul, the work

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: ish ill done; it ish give over. I would have blowed up the town, so

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: Chrish save me, la! in an hour. O, ’tish ill done, ’tish ill done; by

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: my hand, ’tish ill done!

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Captain Macmorris, I beseech you now, will you voutsafe me, look you, a

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: few disputations with you, as partly touching or concerning the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: disciplines of the war, the Roman wars, in the way of argument, look

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: you, and friendly communication; partly to satisfy my opinion, and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: partly for the satisfaction, look you, of my mind, as touching the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: direction of the military discipline; that is the point.

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: It sall be vary gud, gud feith, gud captains bath: and I sall quit you

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: with gud leve, as I may pick occasion; that sall I, marry.

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: It is no time to discourse, so Chrish save me. The day is hot, and the

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: weather, and the wars, and the King, and the Dukes. It is no time to

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: discourse. The town is beseech’d, and the trumpet call us to the

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: breach, and we talk, and, be Chrish, do nothing. ’Tis shame for us all.

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: So God sa’ me, ’tis shame to stand still; it is shame, by my hand; and

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: there is throats to be cut, and works to be done; and there ish nothing

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: done, so Chrish sa’ me, la!

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: By the mess, ere theise eyes of mine take themselves to slomber, I’ll

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: de gud service, or I’ll lig i’ the grund for it; ay, or go to death;

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: and I’ll pay’t as valorously as I may, that sall I suerly do, that is

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: the breff and the long. Marry, I wad full fain heard some question

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: ’tween you tway.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Captain Macmorris, I think, look you, under your correction, there is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: not many of your nation—

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: Of my nation! What ish my nation? Ish a villain, and a bastard, and a

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: knave, and a rascal? What ish my nation? Who talks of my nation?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Look you, if you take the matter otherwise than is meant, Captain

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Macmorris, peradventure I shall think you do not use me with that

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: affability as in discretion you ought to use me, look you, being as

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: good a man as yourself, both in the disciplines of war, and in the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: derivation of my birth, and in other particularities.

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: I do not know you so good a man as myself. So Chrish save me,

lines.speaker: MACMORRIS
lines.text: I will cut off your head.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Gentlemen both, you will mistake each other.

lines.speaker: JAMY
lines.text: Ah! that’s a foul fault.
[_A parley sounded._]

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: The town sounds a parley.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Captain Macmorris, when there is more better opportunity to be

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: required, look you, I will be so bold as to tell you I know the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: disciplines of war; and there is an end.
[_Exeunt._]
The Governor and some citizens on the walls; the English forces below.
Enter King Henry and his train.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How yet resolves the governor of the town?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This is the latest parle we will admit;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore to our best mercy give yourselves,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or like to men proud of destruction

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Defy us to our worst; for, as I am a soldier,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A name that in my thoughts becomes me best,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If I begin the battery once again,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I will not leave the half-achieved Harfleur

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Till in her ashes she lie buried.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The gates of mercy shall be all shut up,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And the flesh’d soldier, rough and hard of heart,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In liberty of bloody hand shall range

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With conscience wide as hell, mowing like grass

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your fresh fair virgins and your flow’ring infants.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is it then to me, if impious War,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Array’d in flames like to the prince of fiends,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do with his smirch’d complexion all fell feats

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Enlink’d to waste and desolation?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is’t to me, when you yourselves are cause,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If your pure maidens fall into the hand

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of hot and forcing violation?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What rein can hold licentious wickedness

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When down the hill he holds his fierce career?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We may as bootless spend our vain command

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon the enraged soldiers in their spoil

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As send precepts to the leviathan

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To come ashore. Therefore, you men of Harfleur,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Take pity of your town and of your people,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whiles yet my soldiers are in my command,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whiles yet the cool and temperate wind of grace

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O’erblows the filthy and contagious clouds

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of heady murder, spoil, and villainy.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If not, why, in a moment look to see

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The blind and bloody soldier with foul hand

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Defile the locks of your shrill-shrieking daughters;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your fathers taken by the silver beards,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And their most reverend heads dash’d to the walls;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your naked infants spitted upon pikes,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whiles the mad mothers with their howls confus’d

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do break the clouds, as did the wives of Jewry

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: At Herod’s bloody-hunting slaughtermen.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What say you? Will you yield, and this avoid,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or, guilty in defence, be thus destroy’d?

lines.speaker: GOVERNOR
lines.text: Our expectation hath this day an end.

lines.speaker: GOVERNOR
lines.text: The Dauphin, whom of succours we entreated,

lines.speaker: GOVERNOR
lines.text: Returns us that his powers are yet not ready

lines.speaker: GOVERNOR
lines.text: To raise so great a siege. Therefore, great King,

lines.speaker: GOVERNOR
lines.text: We yield our town and lives to thy soft mercy.
Enter our gates; dispose of us and ours; For we no longer are defensible.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Open your gates. Come, uncle Exeter,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go you and enter Harfleur; there remain,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And fortify it strongly ’gainst the French.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Use mercy to them all. For us, dear uncle,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The winter coming on, and sickness growing

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon our soldiers, we will retire to Calais.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tonight in Harfleur will we be your guest;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tomorrow for the march are we addrest.
Flourish. The King and his train enter the town.
Enter Katharine and Alice, an old Gentlewoman.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Alice, tu as été en Angleterre, et tu parles bien le langage._

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Un peu, madame._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Je te prie, m’enseignez; il faut que j’apprenne à parler.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Comment appelez-vous la main en anglais?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _La main? Elle est appelée_ de hand.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: De hand. _Et les doigts?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Les doigts? Ma foi, j’oublie les doigts; mais je me souviendrai. Les

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: doigts? Je pense qu’ils sont appelés_ de fingres; _oui_, de fingres.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _La main_, de hand; _les doigts_, de fingres. _Je pense que je suis le

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: bon écolier; j’ai gagné deux mots d’anglais vitement. Comment

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: appelez-vous les ongles?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Les ongles? Nous les appelons_ de nails.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: De nails. _Écoutez; dites-moi, si je parle bien:_ de hand, de fingres,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _et_ de nails.

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _C’est bien dit, madame; il est fort bon anglais._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Dites-moi l’anglais pour le bras._

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: De arm, _madame._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Et le coude?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: D’elbow.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: D’elbow. _Je m’en fais la répétition de tous les mots que vous m’avez

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: appris dès à présent._

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Il est trop difficile, madame, comme je pense._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Excusez-moi, Alice. Écoutez:_ d’hand, de fingres, de nails, d’arm, de

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: bilbow.

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: D’elbow, _madame._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _O Seigneur Dieu, je m’en oublie!_ D’elbow.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Comment appelez-vous le col?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: De nick, _madame._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: De nick. _Et le menton?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: De chin.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: De sin. _Le col_, de nick; _le menton_, de sin.

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Oui. Sauf votre honneur, en vérité, vous prononcez les mots aussi

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: droit que les natifs d’Angleterre._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Je ne doute point d’apprendre, par la grâce de Dieu, et en peu de

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: temps._

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _N’avez-vous pas déjà oublié ce que je vous ai enseigné?_

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Non, je réciterai à vous promptement:_ d’hand, de fingres, de mails,—

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: De nails, _madame._

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: De nails, de arm, de ilbow.

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Sauf votre honneur_, de elbow.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Ainsi dis-je_, d’elbow, de nick, _et_ de sin. _Comment appelez-vous le

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: pied et la robe?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: De foot, _madame; et_ de coun.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: De foot _et_ de coun! _O Seigneur Dieu! ils sont les mots de son

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: mauvais, corruptible, gros, et impudique, et non pour les dames

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: d’honneur d’user. Je ne voudrais prononcer ces mots devant les

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: seigneurs de France pour tout le monde. Foh!_ le foot _et_ le coun!

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Néanmoins, je réciterai une autre fois ma leçon ensemble:_ d’hand, de

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: fingres, de nails, d’arm, d’elbow, de nick, de sin, de foot, de coun.

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Excellent, madame!_

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _C’est assez pour une fois. Allons-nous à dîner._
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the King of France, the Dauphin, the Duke of Bourbon, the Constable of France and others.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: ’Tis certain he hath pass’d the river Somme.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And if he be not fought withal, my lord,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Let us not live in France; let us quit all

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And give our vineyards to a barbarous people.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: _O Dieu vivant_! shall a few sprays of us,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: The emptying of our fathers’ luxury,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Our scions put in wild and savage stock,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Spirt up so suddenly into the clouds,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: And overlook their grafters?

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Normans, but bastard Normans, Norman bastards!

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: _Mort de ma vie_, if they march along

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Unfought withal, but I will sell my dukedom,

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: To buy a slobbery and a dirty farm

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: In that nook-shotten isle of Albion.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: _Dieu de batailles_, where have they this mettle?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Is not their climate foggy, raw, and dull,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: On whom, as in despite, the sun looks pale,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Killing their fruit with frowns? Can sodden water,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: A drench for sur-rein’d jades, their barley-broth,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Decoct their cold blood to such valiant heat?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And shall our quick blood, spirited with wine,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Seem frosty? O, for honour of our land,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Let us not hang like roping icicles

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Upon our houses’ thatch, whiles a more frosty people

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Sweat drops of gallant youth in our rich fields!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Poor we may call them in their native lords.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: By faith and honour,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Our madams mock at us, and plainly say

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Our mettle is bred out, and they will give

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Their bodies to the lust of English youth

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: To new-store France with bastard warriors.

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: They bid us to the English dancing-schools,

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: And teach lavoltas high, and swift corantos;

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Saying our grace is only in our heels,

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: And that we are most lofty runaways.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Where is Montjoy the herald? Speed him hence.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Let him greet England with our sharp defiance.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Up, princes! and, with spirit of honour edged

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: More sharper than your swords, hie to the field!

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Charles Delabreth, High Constable of France;

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: You Dukes of Orleans, Bourbon, and of Berry,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Alençon, Brabant, Bar, and Burgundy;

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Jacques Chatillon, Rambures, Vaudemont,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Beaumont, Grandpré, Roussi, and Fauconbridge,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Foix, Lestrale, Boucicault, and Charolois;

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: High dukes, great princes, barons, lords, and knights,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: For your great seats now quit you of great shames.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Bar Harry England, that sweeps through our land

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: With pennons painted in the blood of Harfleur.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Rush on his host, as doth the melted snow

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Upon the valleys, whose low vassal seat

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: The Alps doth spit and void his rheum upon.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Go down upon him, you have power enough,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: And in a captive chariot into Rouen

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Bring him our prisoner.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: This becomes the great.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Sorry am I his numbers are so few,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: His soldiers sick and famish’d in their march;

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: For I am sure, when he shall see our army,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: He’ll drop his heart into the sink of fear

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And for achievement offer us his ransom.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Therefore, Lord Constable, haste on Montjoy,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: And let him say to England that we send

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: To know what willing ransom he will give.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Prince Dauphin, you shall stay with us in Rouen.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Not so, I do beseech your Majesty.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Be patient, for you shall remain with us.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Now forth, Lord Constable and princes all,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: And quickly bring us word of England’s fall.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Gower and Fluellen, meeting.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: How now, Captain Fluellen! come you from the bridge?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I assure you, there is very excellent services committed at the bridge.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Is the Duke of Exeter safe?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: The Duke of Exeter is as magnanimous as Agamemnon; and a man that I

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: love and honour with my soul, and my heart, and my duty, and my life,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: and my living, and my uttermost power. He is not—God be praised and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: blessed!—any hurt in the world; but keeps the bridge most valiantly,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: with excellent discipline. There is an anchient lieutenant there at the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: pridge, I think in my very conscience he is as valiant a man as Mark

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Antony; and he is a man of no estimation in the world, but I did see

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: him do as gallant service.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: What do you call him?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: He is call’d Anchient Pistol.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: I know him not.
Enter Pistol.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Here is the man.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Captain, I thee beseech to do me favours.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The Duke of Exeter doth love thee well.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Ay, I praise God; and I have merited some love at his hands.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Bardolph, a soldier, firm and sound of heart,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And of buxom valour, hath by cruel fate

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And giddy Fortune’s furious fickle wheel,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: That goddess blind,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: That stands upon the rolling restless stone—

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: By your patience, Anchient Pistol. Fortune is painted blind, with a

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: muffler afore his eyes, to signify to you that Fortune is blind; and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: she is painted also with a wheel, to signify to you, which is the moral

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: of it, that she is turning, and inconstant, and mutability, and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: variation; and her foot, look you, is fixed upon a spherical stone,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: which rolls, and rolls, and rolls. In good truth, the poet makes a most

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: excellent description of it. Fortune is an excellent moral.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Fortune is Bardolph’s foe, and frowns on him;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: For he hath stolen a pax, and hanged must ’a be,—

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: A damned death!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Let gallows gape for dog; let man go free,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And let not hemp his windpipe suffocate.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: But Exeter hath given the doom of death

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: For pax of little price.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Therefore, go speak; the Duke will hear thy voice;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And let not Bardolph’s vital thread be cut

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: With edge of penny cord and vile reproach.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Speak, captain, for his life, and I will thee requite.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Anchient Pistol, I do partly understand your meaning.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Why then, rejoice therefore.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Certainly, anchient, it is not a thing to rejoice at; for if, look you,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: he were my brother, I would desire the Duke to use his good pleasure,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: and put him to execution; for discipline ought to be used.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Die and be damn’d! and _fico_ for thy friendship!

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: It is well.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The fig of Spain.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Very good.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Why, this is an arrant counterfeit rascal. I remember him now; a bawd,

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: a cutpurse.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I’ll assure you, ’a uttered as prave words at the pridge as you shall

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: see in a summer’s day. But it is very well; what he has spoke to me,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: that is well, I warrant you, when time is serve.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Why, ’t is a gull, a fool, a rogue, that now and then goes to the wars,

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: to grace himself at his return into London under the form of a soldier.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: And such fellows are perfect in the great commanders’ names; and they

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: will learn you by rote where services were done; at such and such a

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: sconce, at such a breach, at such a convoy; who came off bravely, who

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: was shot, who disgrac’d, what terms the enemy stood on; and this they

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: con perfectly in the phrase of war, which they trick up with new-tuned

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: oaths: and what a beard of the general’s cut and a horrid suit of the

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: camp will do among foaming bottles and ale-wash’d wits, is wonderful to

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: be thought on. But you must learn to know such slanders of the age, or

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: else you may be marvellously mistook.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I tell you what, Captain Gower; I do perceive he is not the man that he

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: would gladly make show to the world he is. If I find a hole in his

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: coat, I will tell him my mind. [_Drum heard._] Hark you, the King is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: coming, and I must speak with him from the pridge.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Drum and colours. Enter King Henry, Gloucester and his poor soldiers.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: God bless your Majesty!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now, Fluellen! cam’st thou from the bridge?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Ay, so please your Majesty. The Duke of Exeter has very gallantly

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: maintain’d the pridge. The French is gone off, look you; and there is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: gallant and most prave passages. Marry, th’ athversary was have

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: possession of the pridge; but he is enforced to retire, and the Duke of

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Exeter is master of the pridge. I can tell your Majesty, the Duke is a

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: prave man.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What men have you lost, Fluellen?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: The perdition of the athversary hath been very great, reasonable great.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Marry, for my part, I think the Duke hath lost never a man, but one

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: that is like to be executed for robbing a church, one Bardolph, if your

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Majesty know the man. His face is all bubukles, and whelks, and knobs,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: and flames o’ fire; and his lips blows at his nose, and it is like a

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: coal of fire, sometimes plue and sometimes red; but his nose is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: executed, and his fire’s out.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We would have all such offenders so cut off; and we give express

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: charge, that in our marches through the country, there be nothing

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: compell’d from the villages, nothing taken but paid for, none of the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: French upbraided or abused in disdainful language; for when lenity and

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: cruelty play for a kingdom, the gentler gamester is the soonest winner.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tucket. Enter Montjoy.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: You know me by my habit.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well then I know thee. What shall I know of thee?

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: My master’s mind.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Unfold it.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Thus says my King: Say thou to Harry of England: Though we seem’d dead,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: we did but sleep; advantage is a better soldier than rashness. Tell him

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: we could have rebuk’d him at Harfleur, but that we thought not good to

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: bruise an injury till it were full ripe. Now we speak upon our cue, and

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: our voice is imperial. England shall repent his folly, see his

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: weakness, and admire our sufferance. Bid him therefore consider of his

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: ransom; which must proportion the losses we have borne, the subjects we

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: have lost, the disgrace we have digested; which in weight to re-answer,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: his pettishness would bow under. For our losses, his exchequer is too

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: poor; for the effusion of our blood, the muster of his kingdom too

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: faint a number; and for our disgrace, his own person, kneeling at our

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: feet, but a weak and worthless satisfaction. To this add defiance; and

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: tell him, for conclusion, he hath betrayed his followers, whose

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: condemnation is pronounc’d. So far my King and master; so much my

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: office.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is thy name? I know thy quality.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Montjoy.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou dost thy office fairly. Turn thee back,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And tell thy King I do not seek him now,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But could be willing to march on to Calais

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Without impeachment; for, to say the sooth,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Though ’tis no wisdom to confess so much

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Unto an enemy of craft and vantage,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My people are with sickness much enfeebled,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My numbers lessen’d, and those few I have

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Almost no better than so many French;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who when they were in health, I tell thee, herald,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I thought upon one pair of English legs

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Did march three Frenchmen. Yet, forgive me, God,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That I do brag thus! This your air of France

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hath blown that vice in me. I must repent.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go therefore, tell thy master here I am;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My ransom is this frail and worthless trunk,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My army but a weak and sickly guard;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet, God before, tell him we will come on,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Though France himself and such another neighbour

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stand in our way. There’s for thy labour, Montjoy.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go, bid thy master well advise himself.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If we may pass, we will; if we be hind’red,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We shall your tawny ground with your red blood

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Discolour; and so, Montjoy, fare you well.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The sum of all our answer is but this:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We would not seek a battle, as we are;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nor, as we are, we say we will not shun it.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So tell your master.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: I shall deliver so. Thanks to your Highness.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I hope they will not come upon us now.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We are in God’s hands, brother, not in theirs.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: March to the bridge; it now draws toward night.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Beyond the river we’ll encamp ourselves,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And on tomorrow bid them march away.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Constable of France, the Lord Rambures, Orleans, Dauphin with others.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Tut! I have the best armour of the world.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Would it were day!

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: You have an excellent armour; but let my horse have his due.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: It is the best horse of Europe.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: Will it never be morning?

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: My Lord of Orleans, and my Lord High Constable, you talk of horse and

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: armour?

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: You are as well provided of both as any prince in the world.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: What a long night is this! I will not change my horse with any that

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: treads but on four pasterns. Ch’ha! He bounds from the earth, as if his

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: entrails were hairs; _le cheval volant_, the Pegasus, _qui a les

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: narines de feu!_ When I bestride him, I soar, I am a hawk. He trots the

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: air; the earth sings when he touches it; the basest horn of his hoof is

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: more musical than the pipe of Hermes.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: He’s of the colour of the nutmeg.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: And of the heat of the ginger. It is a beast for Perseus. He is pure

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: air and fire; and the dull elements of earth and water never appear in

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: him, but only in patient stillness while his rider mounts him. He is

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: indeed a horse, and all other jades you may call beasts.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Indeed, my lord, it is a most absolute and excellent horse.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: It is the prince of palfreys; his neigh is like the bidding of a

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: monarch, and his countenance enforces homage.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: No more, cousin.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Nay, the man hath no wit that cannot, from the rising of the lark to

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: the lodging of the lamb, vary deserved praise on my palfrey. It is a

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: theme as fluent as the sea; turn the sands into eloquent tongues, and

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: my horse is argument for them all. ’Tis a subject for a sovereign to

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: reason on, and for a sovereign’s sovereign to ride on; and for the

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: world, familiar to us and unknown, to lay apart their particular

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: functions and wonder at him. I once writ a sonnet in his praise and

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: began thus: “Wonder of nature,”—

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: I have heard a sonnet begin so to one’s mistress.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Then did they imitate that which I compos’d to my courser, for my horse

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: is my mistress.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: Your mistress bears well.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Me well; which is the prescript praise and perfection of a good and

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: particular mistress.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Nay, for methought yesterday your mistress shrewdly shook your back.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: So perhaps did yours.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Mine was not bridled.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: O then belike she was old and gentle; and you rode, like a kern of

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Ireland, your French hose off, and in your strait strossers.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: You have good judgment in horsemanship.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Be warn’d by me, then; they that ride so and ride not warily, fall into

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: foul bogs. I had rather have my horse to my mistress.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I had as lief have my mistress a jade.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: I tell thee, Constable, my mistress wears his own hair.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I could make as true a boast as that, if I had a sow to my mistress.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: “_Le chien est retourné à son propre vomissement, et la truie lavée au

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: bourbier_.” Thou mak’st use of anything.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Yet do I not use my horse for my mistress, or any such proverb so

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: little kin to the purpose.

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: My Lord Constable, the armour that I saw in your tent tonight, are

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: those stars or suns upon it?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Stars, my lord.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Some of them will fall tomorrow, I hope.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And yet my sky shall not want.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: That may be, for you bear a many superfluously, and ’twere more honour

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: some were away.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Even as your horse bears your praises; who would trot as well, were

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: some of your brags dismounted.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Would I were able to load him with his desert! Will it never be day? I

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: will trot tomorrow a mile, and my way shall be paved with English

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: faces.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I will not say so, for fear I should be fac’d out of my way. But I

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
