lines.text: would it were morning; for I would fain be about the ears of the

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: English.

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: Who will go to hazard with me for twenty prisoners?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: You must first go yourself to hazard, ere you have them.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: ’Tis midnight; I’ll go arm myself.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: The Dauphin longs for morning.

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: He longs to eat the English.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I think he will eat all he kills.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: By the white hand of my lady, he’s a gallant prince.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Swear by her foot that she may tread out the oath.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: He is simply the most active gentleman of France.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Doing is activity; and he will still be doing.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: He never did harm, that I heard of.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Nor will do none tomorrow. He will keep that good name still.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: I know him to be valiant.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I was told that by one that knows him better than you.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: What’s he?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Marry, he told me so himself; and he said he car’d not who knew it.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: He needs not; it is no hidden virtue in him.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: By my faith, sir, but it is; never anybody saw it but his lackey. ’Tis

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: a hooded valour; and when it appears, it will bate.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: “Ill will never said well.”

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I will cap that proverb with “There is flattery in friendship.”

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: And I will take up that with “Give the devil his due.”

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Well plac’d. There stands your friend for the devil; have at the very

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: eye of that proverb with “A pox of the devil.”

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: You are the better at proverbs, by how much “A fool’s bolt is soon

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: shot.”

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: You have shot over.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: ’Tis not the first time you were overshot.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My Lord High Constable, the English lie within fifteen hundred paces of

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: your tents.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Who hath measur’d the ground?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Lord Grandpré.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: A valiant and most expert gentleman. Would it were day! Alas, poor

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Harry of England, he longs not for the dawning as we do.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: What a wretched and peevish fellow is this King of England, to mope

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: with his fat-brain’d followers so far out of his knowledge!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: If the English had any apprehension, they would run away.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: That they lack; for if their heads had any intellectual armour, they

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: could never wear such heavy head-pieces.

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: That island of England breeds very valiant creatures. Their mastiffs

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: are of unmatchable courage.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: Foolish curs, that run winking into the mouth of a Russian bear and

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: have their heads crush’d like rotten apples! You may as well say,

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: that’s a valiant flea that dare eat his breakfast on the lip of a lion.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Just, just; and the men do sympathize with the mastiffs in robustious

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: and rough coming on, leaving their wits with their wives; and then,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: give them great meals of beef and iron and steel, they will eat like

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: wolves and fight like devils.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: Ay, but these English are shrewdly out of beef.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Then shall we find tomorrow they have only stomachs to eat and none to

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: fight. Now is it time to arm. Come, shall we about it?

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: It is now two o’clock; but, let me see, by ten

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: We shall have each a hundred Englishmen.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Chorus.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Now entertain conjecture of a time

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: When creeping murmur and the poring dark

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Fills the wide vessel of the universe.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: From camp to camp through the foul womb of night

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The hum of either army stilly sounds,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: That the fix’d sentinels almost receive

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The secret whispers of each other’s watch;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Fire answers fire, and through their paly flames

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Each battle sees the other’s umber’d face;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Steed threatens steed, in high and boastful neighs

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Piercing the night’s dull ear; and from the tents

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The armourers, accomplishing the knights,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With busy hammers closing rivets up,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Give dreadful note of preparation.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The country cocks do crow, the clocks do toll,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And the third hour of drowsy morning name.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Proud of their numbers and secure in soul,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The confident and over-lusty French

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Do the low-rated English play at dice;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And chide the cripple tardy-gaited Night

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Who, like a foul and ugly witch, doth limp

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: So tediously away. The poor condemned English,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Like sacrifices, by their watchful fires

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Sit patiently and inly ruminate

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The morning’s danger; and their gesture sad,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Investing lank-lean cheeks and war-worn coats,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Presented them unto the gazing moon

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: So many horrid ghosts. O now, who will behold

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The royal captain of this ruin’d band

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Walking from watch to watch, from tent to tent,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Let him cry, “Praise and glory on his head!”

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: For forth he goes and visits all his host,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Bids them good morrow with a modest smile,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And calls them brothers, friends, and countrymen.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Upon his royal face there is no note

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: How dread an army hath enrounded him;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Nor doth he dedicate one jot of colour

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Unto the weary and all-watched night,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: But freshly looks, and over-bears attaint

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With cheerful semblance and sweet majesty;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: That every wretch, pining and pale before,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Beholding him, plucks comfort from his looks.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: A largess universal like the sun

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: His liberal eye doth give to everyone,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Thawing cold fear, that mean and gentle all

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Behold, as may unworthiness define,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: A little touch of Harry in the night.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And so our scene must to the battle fly,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Where—O for pity!—we shall much disgrace

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With four or five most vile and ragged foils,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Right ill-dispos’d in brawl ridiculous,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The name of Agincourt. Yet sit and see,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Minding true things by what their mock’ries be.
[_Exit._]
Enter King Henry, Bedford and Gloucester.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Gloucester, ’tis true that we are in great danger;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The greater therefore should our courage be.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good morrow, brother Bedford. God Almighty!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: There is some soul of goodness in things evil,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Would men observingly distil it out;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For our bad neighbour makes us early stirrers,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which is both healthful and good husbandry.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Besides, they are our outward consciences,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And preachers to us all, admonishing

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That we should dress us fairly for our end.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thus may we gather honey from the weed,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And make a moral of the devil himself.
Enter Erpingham.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good morrow, old Sir Thomas Erpingham:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A good soft pillow for that good white head

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Were better than a churlish turf of France.

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: Not so, my liege; this lodging likes me better,

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: Since I may say, “Now lie I like a king.”

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ’Tis good for men to love their present pains

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon example; so the spirit is eased;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And when the mind is quick’ned, out of doubt,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The organs, though defunct and dead before,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Break up their drowsy grave and newly move,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With casted slough and fresh legerity.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lend me thy cloak, Sir Thomas. Brothers both,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Commend me to the princes in our camp;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do my good morrow to them, and anon

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Desire them all to my pavilion.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: We shall, my liege.

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: Shall I attend your Grace?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, my good knight;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go with my brothers to my lords of England.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I and my bosom must debate a while,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And then I would no other company.

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: The Lord in heaven bless thee, noble Harry!
[_Exeunt all but King._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: God-a-mercy, old heart! thou speak’st cheerfully.
Enter Pistol.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: _Qui vous là?_

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A friend.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Discuss unto me; art thou officer?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Or art thou base, common, and popular?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am a gentleman of a company.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Trail’st thou the puissant pike?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Even so. What are you?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: As good a gentleman as the Emperor.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then you are a better than the King.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The King’s a bawcock, and a heart of gold,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: A lad of life, an imp of fame;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Of parents good, of fist most valiant.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I kiss his dirty shoe, and from heart-string

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I love the lovely bully. What is thy name?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Harry le Roy.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Le Roy! a Cornish name. Art thou of Cornish crew?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, I am a Welshman.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Know’st thou Fluellen?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Tell him I’ll knock his leek about his pate

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Upon Saint Davy’s day.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do not you wear your dagger in your cap that day, lest he knock that

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: about yours.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Art thou his friend?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And his kinsman too.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The _fico_ for thee, then!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I thank you. God be with you!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: My name is Pistol call’d.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: It sorts well with your fierceness.
Enter Fluellen and Gower.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Captain Fluellen!

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: So! in the name of Jesu Christ, speak lower. It is the greatest

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: admiration in the universal world, when the true and anchient

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: prerogatifes and laws of the wars is not kept. If you would take the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: pains but to examine the wars of Pompey the Great, you shall find, I

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: warrant you, that there is no tiddle taddle nor pibble pabble in

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Pompey’s camp. I warrant you, you shall find the ceremonies of the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: wars, and the cares of it, and the forms of it, and the sobriety of it,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: and the modesty of it, to be otherwise.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Why, the enemy is loud; you hear him all night.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: If the enemy is an ass and a fool and a prating coxcomb, is it meet,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: think you, that we should also, look you, be an ass and a fool and a

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: prating coxcomb? In your own conscience, now?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: I will speak lower.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I pray you and beseech you that you will.
[_Exeunt Gower and Fluellen._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Though it appear a little out of fashion,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: There is much care and valour in this Welshman.
Enter three soldiers, John Bates, Alexander Court and Michael Williams.

lines.speaker: COURT
lines.text: Brother John Bates, is not that the morning which breaks yonder?

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: I think it be; but we have no great cause to desire the approach of

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: day.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: We see yonder the beginning of the day, but I think we shall never see

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: the end of it. Who goes there?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A friend.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Under what captain serve you?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Under Sir Thomas Erpingham.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: A good old commander and a most kind gentleman. I pray you, what thinks

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: he of our estate?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Even as men wreck’d upon a sand, that look to be wash’d off the next

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: tide.

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: He hath not told his thought to the King?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No; nor it is not meet he should. For though I speak it to you, I think

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: the King is but a man as I am. The violet smells to him as it doth to

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: me; the element shows to him as it doth to me; all his senses have but

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: human conditions. His ceremonies laid by, in his nakedness he appears

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: but a man; and though his affections are higher mounted than ours, yet,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: when they stoop, they stoop with the like wing. Therefore, when he sees

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: reason of fears as we do, his fears, out of doubt, be of the same

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: relish as ours are; yet, in reason, no man should possess him with any

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: appearance of fear, lest he, by showing it, should dishearten his army.

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: He may show what outward courage he will; but I believe, as cold a

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: night as ’tis, he could wish himself in Thames up to the neck; and so I

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: would he were, and I by him, at all adventures, so we were quit here.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: By my troth, I will speak my conscience of the King: I think he would

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: not wish himself anywhere but where he is.

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: Then I would he were here alone; so should he be sure to be ransomed,

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: and a many poor men’s lives saved.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I dare say you love him not so ill, to wish him here alone, howsoever

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: you speak this to feel other men’s minds. Methinks I could not die

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: anywhere so contented as in the King’s company, his cause being just

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: and his quarrel honourable.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: That’s more than we know.

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: Ay, or more than we should seek after; for we know enough, if we know

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: we are the King’s subjects. If his cause be wrong, our obedience to the

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: King wipes the crime of it out of us.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: But if the cause be not good, the King himself hath a heavy reckoning

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: to make, when all those legs and arms and heads, chopp’d off in a

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: battle, shall join together at the latter day and cry all, “We died at

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: such a place”; some swearing, some crying for a surgeon, some upon

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: their wives left poor behind them, some upon the debts they owe, some

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: upon their children rawly left. I am afeard there are few die well that

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: die in a battle; for how can they charitably dispose of anything, when

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: blood is their argument? Now, if these men do not die well, it will be

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: a black matter for the King that led them to it; who to disobey were

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: against all proportion of subjection.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So, if a son that is by his father sent about merchandise do sinfully

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: miscarry upon the sea, the imputation of his wickedness, by your rule,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: should be imposed upon his father that sent him; or if a servant, under

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: his master’s command transporting a sum of money, be assailed by

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: robbers and die in many irreconcil’d iniquities, you may call the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: business of the master the author of the servant’s damnation. But this

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: is not so. The King is not bound to answer the particular endings of

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: his soldiers, the father of his son, nor the master of his servant; for

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: they purpose not their death, when they purpose their services.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Besides, there is no king, be his cause never so spotless, if it come

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: to the arbitrement of swords, can try it out with all unspotted

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: soldiers. Some peradventure have on them the guilt of premeditated and

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: contrived murder; some, of beguiling virgins with the broken seals of

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: perjury; some, making the wars their bulwark, that have before gored

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: the gentle bosom of Peace with pillage and robbery. Now, if these men

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: have defeated the law and outrun native punishment, though they can

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: outstrip men, they have no wings to fly from God. War is his beadle,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: war is his vengeance; so that here men are punish’d for before-breach

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: of the King’s laws in now the King’s quarrel. Where they feared the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: death, they have borne life away; and where they would be safe, they

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: perish. Then if they die unprovided, no more is the King guilty of

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: their damnation than he was before guilty of those impieties for the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: which they are now visited. Every subject’s duty is the King’s; but

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: every subject’s soul is his own. Therefore should every soldier in the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: wars do as every sick man in his bed, wash every mote out of his

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: conscience; and dying so, death is to him advantage; or not dying, the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: time was blessedly lost wherein such preparation was gained; and in him

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: that escapes, it were not sin to think that, making God so free an

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: offer, He let him outlive that day to see His greatness and to teach

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: others how they should prepare.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: ’Tis certain, every man that dies ill, the ill upon his own head, the

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: King is not to answer for it.

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: I do not desire he should answer for me; and yet I determine to fight

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: lustily for him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I myself heard the King say he would not be ransom’d.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Ay, he said so, to make us fight cheerfully; but when our throats are

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: cut, he may be ransom’d, and we ne’er the wiser.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If I live to see it, I will never trust his word after.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: You pay him then. That’s a perilous shot out of an elder-gun, that a

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: poor and a private displeasure can do against a monarch! You may as

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: well go about to turn the sun to ice with fanning in his face with a

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: peacock’s feather. You’ll never trust his word after! Come, ’tis a

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: foolish saying.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your reproof is something too round. I should be angry with you, if the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: time were convenient.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Let it be a quarrel between us if you live.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I embrace it.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: How shall I know thee again?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Give me any gage of thine, and I will wear it in my bonnet; then, if

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ever thou dar’st acknowledge it, I will make it my quarrel.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Here’s my glove; give me another of thine.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: There.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: This will I also wear in my cap. If ever thou come to me and say, after

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: tomorrow, “This is my glove,” by this hand I will take thee a box on

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: the ear.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If ever I live to see it, I will challenge it.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Thou dar’st as well be hang’d.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well, I will do it, though I take thee in the King’s company.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Keep thy word; fare thee well.

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: Be friends, you English fools, be friends. We have French quarrels

lines.speaker: BATES
lines.text: enough, if you could tell how to reckon.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Indeed, the French may lay twenty French crowns to one they will beat

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: us, for they bear them on their shoulders; but it is no English treason

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: to cut French crowns, and tomorrow the King himself will be a clipper.
[_Exeunt soldiers._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon the King! Let us our lives, our souls,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Our debts, our careful wives,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Our children, and our sins lay on the King!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We must bear all. O hard condition,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Twin-born with greatness, subject to the breath

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of every fool, whose sense no more can feel

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But his own wringing! What infinite heart’s ease

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Must kings neglect, that private men enjoy!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And what have kings, that privates have not too,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Save ceremony, save general ceremony?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And what art thou, thou idol Ceremony?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What kind of god art thou, that suffer’st more

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of mortal griefs than do thy worshippers?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What are thy rents? What are thy comings in?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O Ceremony, show me but thy worth!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is thy soul of adoration?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Art thou aught else but place, degree, and form,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Creating awe and fear in other men?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Wherein thou art less happy being fear’d

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than they in fearing.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What drink’st thou oft, instead of homage sweet,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But poison’d flattery? O, be sick, great greatness,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And bid thy Ceremony give thee cure!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Think’st thou the fiery fever will go out

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With titles blown from adulation?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Will it give place to flexure and low bending?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Canst thou, when thou command’st the beggar’s knee,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Command the health of it? No, thou proud dream,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That play’st so subtly with a king’s repose;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am a king that find thee, and I know

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ’Tis not the balm, the sceptre, and the ball,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The sword, the mace, the crown imperial,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The intertissued robe of gold and pearl,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The farced title running ’fore the King,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The throne he sits on, nor the tide of pomp

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That beats upon the high shore of this world,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, not all these, thrice-gorgeous Ceremony,—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not all these, laid in bed majestical,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Can sleep so soundly as the wretched slave,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who with a body fill’d and vacant mind

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Gets him to rest, cramm’d with distressful bread,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Never sees horrid night, the child of hell,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But, like a lackey, from the rise to set

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sweats in the eye of Phoebus, and all night

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sleeps in Elysium; next day after dawn,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Doth rise and help Hyperion to his horse,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And follows so the ever-running year,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With profitable labour, to his grave:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, but for ceremony, such a wretch,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Winding up days with toil and nights with sleep,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Had the fore-hand and vantage of a king.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The slave, a member of the country’s peace,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Enjoys it, but in gross brain little wots

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What watch the King keeps to maintain the peace,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose hours the peasant best advantages.
Enter Erpingham.

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: My lord, your nobles, jealous of your absence,

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: Seek through your camp to find you.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good old knight,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Collect them all together at my tent.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I’ll be before thee.

lines.speaker: ERPINGHAM
lines.text: I shall do’t, my lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O God of battles! steel my soldiers’ hearts.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Possess them not with fear. Take from them now

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The sense of reckoning, if the opposed numbers

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Pluck their hearts from them. Not today, O Lord,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, not today, think not upon the fault

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My father made in compassing the crown!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I Richard’s body have interred new,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And on it have bestow’d more contrite tears

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than from it issued forced drops of blood.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Five hundred poor I have in yearly pay,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who twice a day their wither’d hands hold up

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Toward heaven, to pardon blood; and I have built

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Two chantries, where the sad and solemn priests

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sing still for Richard’s soul. More will I do;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Though all that I can do is nothing worth,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Since that my penitence comes after all,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Imploring pardon.
Enter Gloucester.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: My liege!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My brother Gloucester’s voice? Ay;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I know thy errand, I will go with thee.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The day, my friends, and all things stay for me.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Dauphin, Orleans, Rambures and others.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: The sun doth gild our armour; up, my lords!

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: _Monte à cheval!_ My horse, _varlet! laquais_, ha!

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: O brave spirit!

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: _Via, les eaux et terre!_

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: _Rien puis? L’air et feu?_

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: _Cieux_, cousin Orleans.
Enter Constable.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Now, my Lord Constable!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Hark, how our steeds for present service neigh!

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Mount them, and make incision in their hides,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: That their hot blood may spin in English eyes,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: And dout them with superfluous courage, ha!

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: What, will you have them weep our horses’ blood?

lines.speaker: RAMBURES
lines.text: How shall we, then, behold their natural tears?
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The English are embattl’d, you French peers.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: To horse, you gallant princes! straight to horse!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Do but behold yon poor and starved band,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And your fair show shall suck away their souls,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Leaving them but the shales and husks of men.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: There is not work enough for all our hands;

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Scarce blood enough in all their sickly veins

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: To give each naked curtle-axe a stain,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: That our French gallants shall today draw out,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And sheathe for lack of sport. Let us but blow on them,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: The vapour of our valour will o’erturn them.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: ’Tis positive ’gainst all exceptions, lords,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: That our superfluous lackeys and our peasants,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Who in unnecessary action swarm

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: About our squares of battle, were enough

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: To purge this field of such a hilding foe,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Though we upon this mountain’s basis by

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Took stand for idle speculation,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: But that our honours must not. What’s to say?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: A very little little let us do,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And all is done. Then let the trumpets sound

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: The tucket sonance and the note to mount;

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: For our approach shall so much dare the field

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: That England shall crouch down in fear and yield.
Enter Grandpré.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: GRANDPRÉ.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Why do you stay so long, my lords of France?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Yond island carrions, desperate of their bones,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Ill-favouredly become the morning field.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Their ragged curtains poorly are let loose,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And our air shakes them passing scornfully.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Big Mars seems bankrupt in their beggar’d host,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And faintly through a rusty beaver peeps;

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: The horsemen sit like fixed candlesticks

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: With torch-staves in their hand; and their poor jades

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Lob down their heads, drooping the hides and hips,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: The gum down-roping from their pale-dead eyes,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And in their pale dull mouths the gimmal bit

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Lies foul with chew’d grass, still, and motionless;

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And their executors, the knavish crows,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Fly o’er them, all impatient for their hour.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Description cannot suit itself in words

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: To demonstrate the life of such a battle,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: In life so lifeless as it shows itself.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: They have said their prayers, and they stay for death.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Shall we go send them dinners and fresh suits

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: And give their fasting horses provender,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: And after fight with them?

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I stay but for my guard; on to the field!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: I will the banner from a trumpet take,

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: And use it for my haste. Come, come, away!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: The sun is high, and we outwear the day.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Gloucester, Bedford, Exeter, Erpingham, with all his host: Salisbury and Westmorland.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Where is the King?

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: The King himself is rode to view their battle.

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: Of fighting men they have full three-score thousand.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: There’s five to one; besides, they all are fresh.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: God’s arm strike with us! ’tis a fearful odds.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: God be wi’ you, princes all; I’ll to my charge.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: If we no more meet till we meet in heaven,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Then, joyfully, my noble Lord of Bedford,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: My dear Lord Gloucester, and my good Lord Exeter,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And my kind kinsman, warriors all, adieu!

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Farewell, good Salisbury, and good luck go with thee!

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Farewell, kind lord; fight valiantly today!

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And yet I do thee wrong to mind thee of it,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: For thou art fram’d of the firm truth of valour.
[_Exit Salisbury._]

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: He is as full of valour as of kindness,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Princely in both.
Enter the King.

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: O that we now had here

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: But one ten thousand of those men in England

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: That do no work today!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What’s he that wishes so?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My cousin Westmorland? No, my fair cousin.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If we are mark’d to die, we are enough

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To do our country loss; and if to live,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The fewer men, the greater share of honour.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: God’s will! I pray thee, wish not one man more.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: By Jove, I am not covetous for gold,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Nor care I who doth feed upon my cost;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It yearns me not if men my garments wear;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Such outward things dwell not in my desires;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But if it be a sin to covet honour,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I am the most offending soul alive.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: No, faith, my coz, wish not a man from England.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: God’s peace! I would not lose so great an honour

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As one man more, methinks, would share from me

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For the best hope I have. O, do not wish one more!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Rather proclaim it, Westmorland, through my host,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That he which hath no stomach to this fight,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Let him depart. His passport shall be made,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And crowns for convoy put into his purse.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We would not die in that man’s company

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That fears his fellowship to die with us.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This day is call’d the feast of Crispian.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He that outlives this day, and comes safe home,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Will stand a tip-toe when this day is named,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And rouse him at the name of Crispian.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He that shall live this day, and see old age,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Will yearly on the vigil feast his neighbours,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And say, “Tomorrow is Saint Crispian.”

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Then will he strip his sleeve and show his scars,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And say, “These wounds I had on Crispian’s day.”

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Old men forget; yet all shall be forgot,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But he’ll remember with advantages

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What feats he did that day. Then shall our names,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Familiar in his mouth as household words,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Harry the King, Bedford, and Exeter,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Warwick and Talbot, Salisbury and Gloucester,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Be in their flowing cups freshly remembered.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This story shall the good man teach his son;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And Crispin Crispian shall ne’er go by,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: From this day to the ending of the world,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But we in it shall be remembered,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We few, we happy few, we band of brothers.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For he today that sheds his blood with me

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall be my brother; be he ne’er so vile,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This day shall gentle his condition;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And gentlemen in England now abed

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall think themselves accurs’d they were not here,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And hold their manhoods cheap whiles any speaks

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That fought with us upon Saint Crispin’s day.
Enter Salisbury.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: My sovereign lord, bestow yourself with speed.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: The French are bravely in their battles set,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And will with all expedience charge on us.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: All things are ready, if our minds be so.

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: Perish the man whose mind is backward now!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou dost not wish more help from England, coz?

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: God’s will! my liege, would you and I alone,

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: Without more help, could fight this royal battle!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, now thou hast unwish’d five thousand men,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which likes me better than to wish us one.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: You know your places. God be with you all!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Tucket. Enter Montjoy.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Once more I come to know of thee, King Harry,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: If for thy ransom thou wilt now compound,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Before thy most assured overthrow;

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: For certainly thou art so near the gulf,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Thou needs must be englutted. Besides, in mercy,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: The Constable desires thee thou wilt mind

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Thy followers of repentance; that their souls

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: May make a peaceful and a sweet retire

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: From off these fields, where, wretches, their poor bodies

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Must lie and fester.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who hath sent thee now?

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: The Constable of France.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I pray thee, bear my former answer back:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Bid them achieve me and then sell my bones.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good God! why should they mock poor fellows thus?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The man that once did sell the lion’s skin

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: While the beast liv’d, was kill’d with hunting him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A many of our bodies shall no doubt

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Find native graves, upon the which, I trust,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall witness live in brass of this day’s work;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And those that leave their valiant bones in France,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Dying like men, though buried in your dunghills,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They shall be fam’d; for there the sun shall greet them,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And draw their honours reeking up to heaven;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Leaving their earthly parts to choke your clime,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The smell whereof shall breed a plague in France.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Mark then abounding valour in our English,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That being dead, like to the bullet’s grazing,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Break out into a second course of mischief,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Killing in relapse of mortality.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let me speak proudly: tell the Constable

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We are but warriors for the working-day.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Our gayness and our gilt are all besmirch’d

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With rainy marching in the painful field;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: There’s not a piece of feather in our host—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good argument, I hope, we will not fly—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And time hath worn us into slovenry;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But, by the mass, our hearts are in the trim;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And my poor soldiers tell me, yet ere night

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They’ll be in fresher robes, or they will pluck

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The gay new coats o’er the French soldiers’ heads

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And turn them out of service. If they do this—

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As, if God please, they shall,—my ransom then

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Will soon be levied. Herald, save thou thy labour.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come thou no more for ransom, gentle herald.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They shall have none, I swear, but these my joints;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which if they have as I will leave ’em them,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall yield them little, tell the Constable.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: I shall, King Harry. And so fare thee well;

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Thou never shalt hear herald any more.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I fear thou’lt once more come again for ransom.
Enter York.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My lord, most humbly on my knee I beg

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The leading of the vaward.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Take it, brave York. Now, soldiers, march away;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And how thou pleasest, God, dispose the day!
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Excursions. Enter Pistol, French Soldier and Boy.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Yield, cur!

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _Je pense que vous êtes le gentilhomme de bonne qualité._

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: _Qualité? Caleno custore me!_

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Art thou a gentleman?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: What is thy name? Discuss.

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _O Seigneur Dieu!_

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: O, Signieur Dew should be a gentleman.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Perpend my words, O Signieur Dew, and mark:

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: O Signieur Dew, thou diest on point of fox,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Except, O signieur, thou do give to me

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Egregious ransom.

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _O, prenez miséricorde! Ayez pitié de moi!_

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Moy shall not serve; I will have forty moys,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Or I will fetch thy rim out at thy throat

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: In drops of crimson blood.

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _Est-il impossible d’échapper la force de ton bras?_

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Brass, cur!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Thou damned and luxurious mountain goat,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Offer’st me brass?

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _O pardonnez-moi!_

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Say’st thou me so? Is that a ton of moys?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Come hither, boy; ask me this slave in French

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: What is his name.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: _Écoutez. Comment êtes-vous appelé?_

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _Monsieur le Fer._

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: He says his name is Master Fer.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Master Fer! I’ll fer him, and firk him, and ferret him.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Discuss the same in French unto him.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: I do not know the French for fer, and ferret, and firk.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Bid him prepare; for I will cut his throat.

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _Que dit-il, monsieur?_

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: _Il me commande à vous dire que vous faites vous prêt, car ce soldat

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: ici est disposé tout à cette heure de couper votre gorge._

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Owy, cuppele gorge, permafoy,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Peasant, unless thou give me crowns, brave crowns;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Or mangled shalt thou be by this my sword.

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _O, je vous supplie, pour l’amour de Dieu, me pardonner! Je suis le

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: gentilhomme de bonne maison; gardez ma vie, et je vous donnerai deux

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: cents écus._

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: What are his words?

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: He prays you to save his life. He is a gentleman of a good house; and

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: for his ransom he will give you two hundred crowns.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Tell him my fury shall abate, and I

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The crowns will take.

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _Petit monsieur, que dit-il?_

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: _Encore qu’il est contre son jurement de pardonner aucun prisonnier;

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: néanmoins, pour les écus que vous lui avez promis, il est content à

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: vous donner la liberté, le franchisement._

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: _Sur mes genoux je vous donne mille remerciements; et je m’estime

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: heureux que je suis tombé entre les mains d’un chevalier, je pense, le

lines.speaker: FRENCH SOLDIER
lines.text: plus brave, vaillant, et très distingué seigneur d’Angleterre._

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Expound unto me, boy.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: He gives you upon his knees, a thousand thanks; and he esteems himself

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: happy that he hath fallen into the hands of one, as he thinks, the most

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: brave, valorous, and thrice-worthy _seigneur_ of England.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: As I suck blood, I will some mercy show.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Follow me!

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: _Suivez-vous le grand capitaine._
[_Exeunt Pistol and French Soldier._]

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: I did never know so full a voice issue from so empty a heart; but the

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: saying is true, “The empty vessel makes the greatest sound.” Bardolph

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: and Nym had ten times more valour than this roaring devil i’ the old

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: play, that everyone may pare his nails with a wooden dagger; and they

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: are both hang’d; and so would this be, if he durst steal anything

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: adventurously. I must stay with the lackeys with the luggage of our

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: camp. The French might have a good prey of us, if he knew of it; for

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: there is none to guard it but boys.
[_Exit._]
Enter Constable, Orleans, Bourbon, Dauphin and Rambures.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: _O diable!_

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: _O Seigneur! le jour est perdu, tout est perdu!_

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: _Mort de ma vie!_ all is confounded, all!

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Reproach and everlasting shame

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Sits mocking in our plumes.
[_A short alarum._]

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: _O méchante Fortune!_ Do not run away.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Why, all our ranks are broke.

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: O perdurable shame! Let’s stab ourselves,

lines.speaker: DAUPHIN
lines.text: Be these the wretches that we play’d at dice for?

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: Is this the king we sent to for his ransom?

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Shame and eternal shame, nothing but shame!

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Let’s die in honour! Once more back again!

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: And he that will not follow Bourbon now,

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Let him go hence, and with his cap in hand,

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Like a base pandar, hold the chamber door

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Whilst by a slave, no gentler than my dog,

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: His fairest daughter is contaminated.

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Disorder, that hath spoil’d us, friend us now!

lines.speaker: CONSTABLE
lines.text: Let us on heaps go offer up our lives.

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: We are enough yet living in the field

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: To smother up the English in our throngs,

lines.speaker: ORLEANS
lines.text: If any order might be thought upon.

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: The devil take order now! I’ll to the throng.

lines.speaker: BOURBON
lines.text: Let life be short, else shame will be too long.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Enter King Henry and his train, with prisoners.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well have we done, thrice valiant countrymen.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But all’s not done; yet keep the French the field.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The Duke of York commends him to your Majesty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lives he, good uncle? Thrice within this hour

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I saw him down; thrice up again, and fighting.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: From helmet to the spur all blood he was.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: In which array, brave soldier, doth he lie,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Larding the plain; and by his bloody side,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Yoke-fellow to his honour-owing wounds,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The noble Earl of Suffolk also lies.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Suffolk first died; and York, all haggled over,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Comes to him, where in gore he lay insteeped,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And takes him by the beard; kisses the gashes

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That bloodily did yawn upon his face.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He cries aloud, “Tarry, my cousin Suffolk!

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: My soul shall thine keep company to heaven;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Tarry, sweet soul, for mine, then fly abreast,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: As in this glorious and well-foughten field

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: We kept together in our chivalry.”

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Upon these words I came and cheer’d him up.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He smil’d me in the face, raught me his hand,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And, with a feeble gripe, says, “Dear my lord,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Commend my service to my sovereign.”

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: So did he turn and over Suffolk’s neck

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: He threw his wounded arm and kiss’d his lips;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And so espous’d to death, with blood he seal’d

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: A testament of noble-ending love.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The pretty and sweet manner of it forc’d

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Those waters from me which I would have stopp’d;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: But I had not so much of man in me,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And all my mother came into mine eyes

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And gave me up to tears.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I blame you not;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For, hearing this, I must perforce compound

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With mistful eyes, or they will issue too.
[_Alarum._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But hark! what new alarum is this same?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The French have reinforc’d their scatter’d men.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then every soldier kill his prisoners;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Give the word through.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Fluellen and Gower.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Kill the poys and the luggage! ’Tis expressly against the law of arms.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: ’Tis as arrant a piece of knavery, mark you now, as can be offer’t; in

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: your conscience, now, is it not?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: ’Tis certain there’s not a boy left alive; and the cowardly rascals

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: that ran from the battle ha’ done this slaughter. Besides, they have

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: burned and carried away all that was in the King’s tent; wherefore the

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: King, most worthily, hath caus’d every soldier to cut his prisoner’s

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: throat. O, ’tis a gallant king!

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Ay, he was porn at Monmouth, Captain Gower. What call you the town’s

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: name where Alexander the Pig was born?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Alexander the Great.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Why, I pray you, is not pig great? The pig, or the great, or the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: mighty, or the huge, or the magnanimous, are all one reckonings, save

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: the phrase is a little variations.

lines.speaker: GOWER

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Philip of Macedon, as I take it.

lines.text: I think it is in Macedon where Alexander is porn. I tell you, Captain,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: if you look in the maps of the ’orld, I warrant you sall find, in the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: comparisons between Macedon and Monmouth, that the situations, look

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: you, is both alike. There is a river in Macedon; and there is also

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: moreover a river at Monmouth; it is call’d Wye at Monmouth; but it is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: out of my prains what is the name of the other river; but ’tis all one,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: ’tis alike as my fingers is to my fingers, and there is salmons in

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: both. If you mark Alexander’s life well, Harry of Monmouth’s life is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: come after it indifferent well; for there is figures in all things.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Alexander, God knows, and you know, in his rages, and his furies, and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: his wraths, and his cholers, and his moods, and his displeasures, and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: his indignations, and also being a little intoxicates in his prains,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: did, in his ales and his angers, look you, kill his best friend,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Cleitus.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Our King is not like him in that. He never kill’d any of his friends.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: It is not well done, mark you now, to take the tales out of my mouth,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: ere it is made and finished. I speak but in the figures and comparisons

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: of it. As Alexander kill’d his friend Cleitus, being in his ales and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: his cups; so also Harry Monmouth, being in his right wits and his good

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: judgements, turn’d away the fat knight with the great belly doublet. He

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: was full of jests, and gipes, and knaveries, and mocks; I have forgot

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: his name.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Sir John Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: That is he. I’ll tell you there is good men porn at Monmouth.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Here comes his Majesty.
Alarum. Enter King Henry and forces; Warwick, Gloucester, Exeter with prisoners. Flourish.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I was not angry since I came to France

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Until this instant. Take a trumpet, herald;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ride thou unto the horsemen on yond hill.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If they will fight with us, bid them come down,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or void the field; they do offend our sight.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If they’ll do neither, we will come to them,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And make them skirr away, as swift as stones

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Enforced from the old Assyrian slings.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Besides, we’ll cut the throats of those we have,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And not a man of them that we shall take

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall taste our mercy. Go and tell them so.
Enter Montjoy.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Here comes the herald of the French, my liege.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His eyes are humbler than they us’d to be.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now! what means this, herald? Know’st thou not

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That I have fin’d these bones of mine for ransom?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Com’st thou again for ransom?

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: No, great King;

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: I come to thee for charitable license,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: That we may wander o’er this bloody field

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: To book our dead, and then to bury them;

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: To sort our nobles from our common men.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: For many of our princes—woe the while!—

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Lie drown’d and soak’d in mercenary blood;

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: So do our vulgar drench their peasant limbs

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: In blood of princes; and their wounded steeds

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Fret fetlock deep in gore, and with wild rage

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Yerk out their armed heels at their dead masters,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Killing them twice. O, give us leave, great King,

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: To view the field in safety, and dispose

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: Of their dead bodies!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I tell thee truly, herald,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I know not if the day be ours or no;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For yet a many of your horsemen peer

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And gallop o’er the field.

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: The day is yours.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Praised be God, and not our strength, for it!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is this castle call’d that stands hard by?

lines.speaker: MONTJOY
lines.text: They call it Agincourt.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then call we this the field of Agincourt,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Fought on the day of Crispin Crispianus.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Your grandfather of famous memory, an’t please your Majesty, and your

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: great-uncle Edward the Plack Prince of Wales, as I have read in the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: chronicles, fought a most prave pattle here in France.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They did, Fluellen.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Your Majesty says very true. If your Majesties is rememb’red of it, the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Welshmen did good service in garden where leeks did grow, wearing leeks

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: in their Monmouth caps; which, your Majesty know, to this hour is an

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: honourable badge of the service; and I do believe your Majesty takes no

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: scorn to wear the leek upon Saint Tavy’s day.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I wear it for a memorable honour;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For I am Welsh, you know, good countryman.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: All the water in Wye cannot wash your Majesty’s Welsh plood out of your

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: pody, I can tell you that. Got pless it and preserve it, as long as it

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: pleases His grace, and His majesty too!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thanks, good my countryman.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: By Jeshu, I am your Majesty’s countryman, I care not who know it. I

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: will confess it to all the ’orld. I need not be asham’d of your

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Majesty, praised be God, so long as your Majesty is an honest man.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: God keep me so!
Enter Williams.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Our heralds go with him;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Bring me just notice of the numbers dead

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: On both our parts. Call yonder fellow hither.
[_Exeunt Heralds with Montjoy._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Soldier, you must come to the King.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Soldier, why wear’st thou that glove in thy cap?

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: An’t please your Majesty, ’tis the gage of one that I should fight

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: withal, if he be alive.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: An Englishman?

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: An’t please your Majesty, a rascal that swagger’d with me last night;

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: who, if alive and ever dare to challenge this glove, I have sworn to

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: take him a box o’ the ear; or if I can see my glove in his cap, which

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: he swore, as he was a soldier, he would wear if alive, I will strike it

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: out soundly.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What think you, Captain Fluellen, is it fit this soldier keep his oath?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: He is a craven and a villain else, an’t please your Majesty, in my

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: conscience.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: It may be his enemy is a gentlemen of great sort, quite from the answer

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: of his degree.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Though he be as good a gentleman as the devil is, as Lucifier and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Belzebub himself, it is necessary, look your Grace, that he keep his

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: vow and his oath. If he be perjur’d, see you now, his reputation is as

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: arrant a villain and a Jacksauce, as ever his black shoe trod upon

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: God’s ground and His earth, in my conscience, la!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then keep thy vow, sirrah, when thou meet’st the fellow.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: So I will, my liege, as I live.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who serv’st thou under?

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Under Captain Gower, my liege.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Gower is a good captain, and is good knowledge and literatured in the

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: wars.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Call him hither to me, soldier.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: I will, my liege.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here, Fluellen; wear thou this favour for me and stick it in thy cap.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When Alençon and myself were down together, I pluck’d this glove from

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: his helm. If any man challenge this, he is a friend to Alençon, and an

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: enemy to our person. If thou encounter any such, apprehend him, an thou

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: dost me love.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Your Grace does me as great honours as can be desir’d in the hearts of

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: his subjects. I would fain see the man, that has but two legs, that

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: shall find himself aggrief’d at this glove; that is all. But I would

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: fain see it once, an please God of His grace that I might see.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Know’st thou Gower?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: He is my dear friend, an please you.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Pray thee, go seek him, and bring him to my tent.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I will fetch him.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My Lord of Warwick, and my brother Gloucester,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Follow Fluellen closely at the heels.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The glove which I have given him for a favour

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: May haply purchase him a box o’ the ear.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: It is the soldier’s; I by bargain should

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Wear it myself. Follow, good cousin Warwick.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If that the soldier strike him, as I judge

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: By his blunt bearing he will keep his word,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Some sudden mischief may arise of it;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For I do know Fluellen valiant

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, touch’d with choler, hot as gunpowder,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And quickly will return an injury.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Follow, and see there be no harm between them.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go you with me, uncle of Exeter.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Gower and Williams.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: I warrant it is to knight you, Captain.
Enter Fluellen.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: God’s will and his pleasure, captain, I beseech you now, come apace to

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: the King. There is more good toward you peradventure than is in your

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: knowledge to dream of.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Sir, know you this glove?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Know the glove! I know the glove is a glove.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: I know this; and thus I challenge it.
[_Strikes him._]

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: ’Sblood! an arrant traitor as any is in the universal world, or in

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: France, or in England!

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: How now, sir! you villain!

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Do you think I’ll be forsworn?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Stand away, Captain Gower. I will give treason his payment into plows,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I warrant you.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: I am no traitor.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: That’s a lie in thy throat. I charge you in his Majesty’s name,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: apprehend him; he’s a friend of the Duke Alençon’s.
Enter Warwick and Gloucester.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How now, how now! what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: My lord of Warwick, here is—praised be God for it!—a most contagious

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: treason come to light, look you, as you shall desire in a summer’s day.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Here is his Majesty.
Enter King Henry and Exeter.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How now! what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: My liege, here is a villain and a traitor, that, look your Grace, has

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: struck the glove which your Majesty is take out of the helmet of

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Alençon.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: My liege, this was my glove; here is the fellow of it; and he that I

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: gave it to in change promis’d to wear it in his cap. I promis’d to

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: strike him, if he did. I met this man with my glove in his cap, and I

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: have been as good as my word.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Your Majesty hear now, saving your Majesty’s manhood, what an arrant,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: rascally, beggarly, lousy knave it is. I hope your Majesty is pear me

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: testimony and witness, and will avouchment, that this is the glove of

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Alençon that your Majesty is give me; in your conscience, now?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Give me thy glove, soldier. Look, here is the fellow of it.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ’Twas I, indeed, thou promisedst to strike;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And thou hast given me most bitter terms.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: An it please your Majesty, let his neck answer for it, if there is any

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: martial law in the world.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How canst thou make me satisfaction?

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: All offences, my lord, come from the heart. Never came any from mine

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: that might offend your Majesty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: It was ourself thou didst abuse.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Your Majesty came not like yourself. You appear’d to me but as a common

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: man; witness the night, your garments, your lowliness; and what your

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: Highness suffer’d under that shape, I beseech you take it for your own

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: fault and not mine; for had you been as I took you for, I made no

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: offence; therefore, I beseech your Highness, pardon me.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here, uncle Exeter, fill this glove with crowns,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And give it to this fellow. Keep it, fellow;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And wear it for an honour in thy cap

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Till I do challenge it. Give him his crowns;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, captain, you must needs be friends with him.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: By this day and this light, the fellow has mettle enough in his belly.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Hold, there is twelve pence for you; and I pray you to serve God, and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: keep you out of prawls, and prabbles, and quarrels, and dissensions,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: and, I warrant you, it is the better for you.

lines.speaker: WILLIAMS
lines.text: I will none of your money.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: It is with a good will; I can tell you, it will serve you to mend your

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: shoes. Come, wherefore should you be so pashful? Your shoes is not so

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: good. ’Tis a good silling, I warrant you, or I will change it.
Enter an English Herald.

lines.text: Now, herald, are the dead numb’red?

lines.speaker: HERALD
lines.text: Here is the number of the slaught’red French.
