lines.text: What prisoners of good sort are taken, uncle?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Charles Duke of Orleans, nephew to the King;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: John Duke of Bourbon, and Lord Boucicault:

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Of other lords and barons, knights and squires,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Full fifteen hundred, besides common men.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This note doth tell me of ten thousand French

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That in the field lie slain; of princes, in this number,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And nobles bearing banners, there lie dead

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: One hundred twenty-six; added to these,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of knights, esquires, and gallant gentlemen,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Eight thousand and four hundred; of the which,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Five hundred were but yesterday dubb’d knights;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So that, in these ten thousand they have lost,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: There are but sixteen hundred mercenaries;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The rest are princes, barons, lords, knights, squires,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And gentlemen of blood and quality.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The names of those their nobles that lie dead:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Charles Delabreth, High Constable of France;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Jacques of Chatillon, Admiral of France;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The master of the Crossbows, Lord Rambures;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Great Master of France, the brave Sir Guichard Dauphin,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: John, Duke of Alençon, Anthony, Duke of Brabant,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The brother to the Duke of Burgundy,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And Edward, Duke of Bar; of lusty earls,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Grandpré and Roussi, Fauconbridge and Foix,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Beaumont and Marle, Vaudemont and Lestrale.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Here was a royal fellowship of death!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where is the number of our English dead?
[_Herald gives him another paper._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Edward the Duke of York, the Earl of Suffolk,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sir Richard Ketly, Davy Gam, esquire;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: None else of name; and of all other men

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But five and twenty.—O God, thy arm was here;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And not to us, but to thy arm alone,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ascribe we all! When, without stratagem,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But in plain shock and even play of battle,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Was ever known so great and little loss

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: On one part and on the other? Take it, God,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For it is none but thine!

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: ’Tis wonderful!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come, go we in procession to the village;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And be it death proclaimed through our host

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To boast of this or take that praise from God

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which is His only.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Is it not lawful, an please your Majesty, to tell how many is kill’d?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yes, Captain; but with this acknowledgment,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That God fought for us.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Yes, my conscience, He did us great good.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do we all holy rites.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let there be sung _Non nobis_ and _Te Deum_,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The dead with charity enclos’d in clay,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And then to Calais; and to England then,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where ne’er from France arriv’d more happy men.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Chorus.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Vouchsafe to those that have not read the story,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: That I may prompt them; and of such as have,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: I humbly pray them to admit the excuse

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Of time, of numbers, and due course of things,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Which cannot in their huge and proper life

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Be here presented. Now we bear the King

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Toward Calais; grant him there; there seen,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Heave him away upon your winged thoughts

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Athwart the sea. Behold, the English beach

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Pales in the flood with men, with wives and boys,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Whose shouts and claps out-voice the deep-mouth’d sea,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Which like a mighty whiffler ’fore the King

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Seems to prepare his way. So let him land,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And solemnly see him set on to London.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: So swift a pace hath thought that even now

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: You may imagine him upon Blackheath,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Where that his lords desire him to have borne

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: His bruised helmet and his bended sword

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Before him through the city. He forbids it,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Being free from vainness and self-glorious pride;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Giving full trophy, signal, and ostent

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Quite from himself to God. But now behold,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: In the quick forge and working-house of thought,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: How London doth pour out her citizens!

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The mayor and all his brethren in best sort,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Like to the senators of th’ antique Rome,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: With the plebeians swarming at their heels,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Go forth and fetch their conquering Caesar in;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: As, by a lower but loving likelihood,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Were now the general of our gracious empress,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: As in good time he may, from Ireland coming,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Bringing rebellion broached on his sword,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: How many would the peaceful city quit,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: To welcome him! Much more, and much more cause,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Did they this Harry. Now in London place him;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: As yet the lamentation of the French

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Invites the King of England’s stay at home,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The Emperor’s coming in behalf of France,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: To order peace between them;—and omit

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: All the occurrences, whatever chanc’d,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Till Harry’s back-return again to France.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: There must we bring him; and myself have play’d

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: The interim, by rememb’ring you ’tis past.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Then brook abridgement, and your eyes advance

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: After your thoughts, straight back again to France.
[_Exit._]
Enter Fluellen and Gower.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Nay, that’s right; but why wear you your leek today?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Saint Davy’s day is past.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: There is occasions and causes why and wherefore in all things. I will

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: tell you ass my friend, Captain Gower. The rascally, scald, beggarly,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: lousy, pragging knave, Pistol, which you and yourself and all the world

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: know to be no petter than a fellow, look you now, of no merits, he is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: come to me and prings me pread and salt yesterday, look you, and bid me

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: eat my leek. It was in a place where I could not breed no contention

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: with him; but I will be so bold as to wear it in my cap till I see him

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: once again, and then I will tell him a little piece of my desires.
Enter Pistol.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Why, here he comes, swelling like a turkey-cock.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: ’Tis no matter for his swellings nor his turkey-cocks. God pless you,

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Anchient Pistol! you scurvy, lousy knave, God pless you!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Ha! art thou bedlam? Dost thou thirst, base Trojan,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: To have me fold up Parca’s fatal web?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Hence! I am qualmish at the smell of leek.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I peseech you heartily, scurfy, lousy knave, at my desires, and my

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: requests, and my petitions, to eat, look you, this leek. Because, look

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: you, you do not love it, nor your affections and your appetites and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: your digestions does not agree with it, I would desire you to eat it.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Not for Cadwallader and all his goats.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: There is one goat for you. [_Strikes him._] Will you be so good, scald

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: knave, as eat it?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Base Trojan, thou shalt die.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: You say very true, scald knave, when God’s will is. I will desire you

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: to live in the mean time, and eat your victuals. Come, there is sauce

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: for it. [_Strikes him._] You call’d me yesterday mountain-squire; but I

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: will make you today a squire of low degree. I pray you, fall to; if you

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: can mock a leek, you can eat a leek.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Enough, captain; you have astonish’d him.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: I say, I will make him eat some part of my leek, or I will peat his

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: pate four days. Bite, I pray you; it is good for your green wound and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: your ploody coxcomb.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Must I bite?

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Yes, certainly, and out of doubt and out of question too, and

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: ambiguities.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: By this leek, I will most horribly revenge. I eat and eat, I swear—

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Eat, I pray you. Will you have some more sauce to your leek? There is

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: not enough leek to swear by.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Quiet thy cudgel; thou dost see I eat.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Much good do you, scald knave, heartily. Nay, pray you, throw none

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: away; the skin is good for your broken coxcomb. When you take occasions

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: to see leeks hereafter, I pray you, mock at ’em; that is all.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Ay, leeks is good. Hold you, there is a groat to heal your pate.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Me a groat!

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: Yes, verily and in truth you shall take it; or I have another leek in

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: my pocket, which you shall eat.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I take thy groat in earnest of revenge.

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: If I owe you anything I will pay you in cudgels. You shall be a

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: woodmonger, and buy nothing of me but cudgels. God be wi’ you, and keep

lines.speaker: FLUELLEN
lines.text: you, and heal your pate.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: All hell shall stir for this.

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Go, go; you are a couterfeit cowardly knave. Will you mock at an

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: ancient tradition, begun upon an honourable respect, and worn as a

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: memorable trophy of predeceased valour, and dare not avouch in your

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: deeds any of your words? I have seen you gleeking and galling at this

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: gentleman twice or thrice. You thought, because he could not speak

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: English in the native garb, he could not therefore handle an English

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: cudgel. You find it otherwise; and henceforth let a Welsh correction

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: teach you a good English condition. Fare ye well.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Doth Fortune play the huswife with me now?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: News have I, that my Doll is dead i’ the spital

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Of malady of France;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And there my rendezvous is quite cut off.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Old I do wax; and from my weary limbs

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Honour is cudgell’d. Well, bawd I’ll turn,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And something lean to cutpurse of quick hand.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: To England will I steal, and there I’ll steal;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And patches will I get unto these cudgell’d scars,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And swear I got them in the Gallia wars.
[_Exit._]

Enter at one door, King Henry, Exeter, Bedford, Warwick, Gloucester, Westmorland, Clarence, Huntingdon and other Lords. At another, Queen Isabel, the French King, the Princess Katharine, Alice, and other Ladies; the Duke of Burgundy and other French.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Peace to this meeting, wherefore we are met!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Unto our brother France, and to our sister,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Health and fair time of day; joy and good wishes

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To our most fair and princely cousin Katharine;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, as a branch and member of this royalty,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: By whom this great assembly is contriv’d,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We do salute you, Duke of Burgundy;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, princes French, and peers, health to you all!

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Right joyous are we to behold your face,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Most worthy brother England; fairly met!

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: So are you, princes English, every one.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: So happy be the issue, brother England,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Of this good day and of this gracious meeting

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: As we are now glad to behold your eyes;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Your eyes, which hitherto have borne in them

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Against the French that met them in their bent

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: The fatal balls of murdering basilisks.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: The venom of such looks, we fairly hope,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Have lost their quality; and that this day

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Shall change all griefs and quarrels into love.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To cry amen to that, thus we appear.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: You English princes all, I do salute you.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: My duty to you both, on equal love,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Great Kings of France and England! That I have labour’d,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: With all my wits, my pains, and strong endeavours,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: To bring your most imperial Majesties

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Unto this bar and royal interview,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Your mightiness on both parts best can witness.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Since then my office hath so far prevail’d

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: That, face to face and royal eye to eye,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: You have congreeted, let it not disgrace me

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: If I demand, before this royal view,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: What rub or what impediment there is,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Why that the naked, poor, and mangled Peace,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Dear nurse of arts, plenties, and joyful births,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Should not in this best garden of the world,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Our fertile France, put up her lovely visage?

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Alas, she hath from France too long been chas’d,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And all her husbandry doth lie on heaps,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Corrupting in it own fertility.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Her vine, the merry cheerer of the heart,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Unpruned dies; her hedges even-pleach’d,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Like prisoners wildly overgrown with hair,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Put forth disorder’d twigs; her fallow leas

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: The darnel, hemlock, and rank fumitory,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Doth root upon, while that the coulter rusts

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: That should deracinate such savagery;

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: The even mead, that erst brought sweetly forth

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: The freckled cowslip, burnet, and green clover,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Wanting the scythe, all uncorrected, rank,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Conceives by idleness, and nothing teems

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: But hateful docks, rough thistles, kecksies, burs,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Losing both beauty and utility;

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And as our vineyards, fallows, meads, and hedges,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Defective in their natures, grow to wildness.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Even so our houses and ourselves and children

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Have lost, or do not learn for want of time,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: The sciences that should become our country;

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: But grow like savages,—as soldiers will

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: That nothing do but meditate on blood,—

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: To swearing and stern looks, diffus’d attire,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And everything that seems unnatural.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Which to reduce into our former favour

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: You are assembled; and my speech entreats

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: That I may know the let, why gentle Peace

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Should not expel these inconveniences

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And bless us with her former qualities.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If, Duke of Burgundy, you would the peace,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whose want gives growth to the imperfections

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which you have cited, you must buy that peace

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With full accord to all our just demands;

lines.text: Whose tenours and particular effects

lines.text: You have enschedul’d briefly in your hands.

lines.text: The King hath heard them; to the which as yet

lines.text: There is no answer made.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Well, then, the peace,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Which you before so urg’d, lies in his answer.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: I have but with a cursorary eye

lines.text: O’erglanc’d the articles. Pleaseth your Grace

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: To appoint some of your council presently

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: To sit with us once more, with better heed

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: To re-survey them, we will suddenly

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Pass our accept and peremptory answer.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Brother, we shall. Go, uncle Exeter,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And brother Clarence, and you, brother Gloucester,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Warwick, and Huntington, go with the King;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And take with you free power to ratify,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Augment, or alter, as your wisdoms best

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall see advantageable for our dignity,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Anything in or out of our demands,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And we’ll consign thereto. Will you, fair sister,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go with the princes, or stay here with us?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Our gracious brother, I will go with them.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Haply a woman’s voice may do some good,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: When articles too nicely urg’d be stood on.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet leave our cousin Katharine here with us:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: She is our capital demand, compris’d

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Within the fore-rank of our articles.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: She hath good leave.
[_Exeunt all except Henry, Katharine and Alice._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Fair Katharine, and most fair,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Will you vouchsafe to teach a soldier terms

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Such as will enter at a lady’s ear

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And plead his love-suit to her gentle heart?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Your Majesty shall mock me; I cannot speak your England.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O fair Katharine, if you will love me soundly with your French heart, I

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: will be glad to hear you confess it brokenly with your English tongue.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do you like me, Kate?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Pardonnez-moi_, I cannot tell wat is “like me.”

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: An angel is like you, Kate, and you are like an angel.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Que dit-il? Que je suis semblable à les anges?_

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Oui, vraiment, sauf votre Grâce, ainsi dit-il._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I said so, dear Katharine; and I must not blush to affirm it.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _O bon Dieu! les langues des hommes sont pleines de tromperies._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What says she, fair one? That the tongues of men are full of deceits?

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Oui_, dat de tongues of de mans is be full of deceits: dat is de

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: Princess.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The Princess is the better Englishwoman. I’ faith, Kate, my wooing is

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: fit for thy understanding. I am glad thou canst speak no better

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: English; for if thou couldst, thou wouldst find me such a plain king

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: that thou wouldst think I had sold my farm to buy my crown. I know no

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ways to mince it in love, but directly to say, “I love you”; then if

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: you urge me farther than to say, “Do you in faith?” I wear out my suit.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Give me your answer; i’ faith, do; and so clap hands and a bargain. How

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: say you, lady?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Sauf votre honneur_, me understand well.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Marry, if you would put me to verses, or to dance for your sake, Kate,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: why you undid me; for the one, I have neither words nor measure, and

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: for the other I have no strength in measure, yet a reasonable measure

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: in strength. If I could win a lady at leap-frog, or by vaulting into my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: saddle with my armour on my back, under the correction of bragging be

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: it spoken, I should quickly leap into a wife. Or if I might buffet for

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: my love, or bound my horse for her favours, I could lay on like a

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: butcher and sit like a jack-an-apes, never off. But, before God, Kate,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I cannot look greenly, nor gasp out my eloquence, nor I have no cunning

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: in protestation; only downright oaths, which I never use till urg’d,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: nor never break for urging. If thou canst love a fellow of this temper,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Kate, whose face is not worth sunburning, that never looks in his glass

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: for love of anything he sees there, let thine eye be thy cook. I speak

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: to thee plain soldier. If thou canst love me for this, take me; if not,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: to say to thee that I shall die, is true; but for thy love, by the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Lord, no; yet I love thee too. And while thou liv’st, dear Kate, take a

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: fellow of plain and uncoined constancy; for he perforce must do thee

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: right, because he hath not the gift to woo in other places; for these

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: fellows of infinite tongue, that can rhyme themselves into ladies’

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: favours, they do always reason themselves out again. What! a speaker is

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: but a prater: a rhyme is but a ballad. A good leg will fall; a straight

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: back will stoop; a black beard will turn white; a curl’d pate will grow

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: bald; a fair face will wither; a full eye will wax hollow; but a good

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: heart, Kate, is the sun and the moon; or rather the sun and not the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: moon; for it shines bright and never changes, but keeps his course

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: truly. If thou would have such a one, take me; and take me, take a

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: soldier; take a soldier, take a king. And what say’st thou then to my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: love? Speak, my fair, and fairly, I pray thee.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Is it possible dat I should love de enemy of France?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No; it is not possible you should love the enemy of France, Kate; but,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: in loving me, you should love the friend of France; for I love France

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: so well that I will not part with a village of it, I will have it all

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: mine; and, Kate, when France is mine and I am yours, then yours is

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: France and you are mine.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: I cannot tell wat is dat.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, Kate? I will tell thee in French; which I am sure will hang upon my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: tongue like a new-married wife about her husband’s neck, hardly to be

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: shook off. _Je quand sur le possession de France, et quand vous avez le

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: possession de moi_,—let me see, what then? Saint Denis be my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: speed!—_donc votre est France, et vous êtes mienne._ It is as easy for

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: me, Kate, to conquer the kingdom as to speak so much more French. I

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: shall never move thee in French, unless it be to laugh at me.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Sauf votre honneur, le français que vous parlez, il est meilleur que

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: l’anglais lequel je parle._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No, faith, is’t not, Kate; but thy speaking of my tongue, and I thine,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: most truly-falsely, must needs be granted to be much at one. But, Kate,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: dost thou understand thus much English: canst thou love me?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: I cannot tell.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Can any of your neighbours tell, Kate? I’ll ask them. Come, I know thou

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: lovest me; and at night, when you come into your closet, you’ll

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: question this gentlewoman about me; and I know, Kate, you will to her

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: dispraise those parts in me that you love with your heart. But, good

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Kate, mock me mercifully; the rather, gentle princess, because I love

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: thee cruelly. If ever thou beest mine, Kate, as I have a saving faith

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: within me tells me thou shalt, I get thee with scambling, and thou must

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: therefore needs prove a good soldier-breeder. Shall not thou and I,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: between Saint Denis and Saint George, compound a boy, half French, half

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: English, that shall go to Constantinople and take the Turk by the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: beard? Shall we not? What say’st thou, my fair flower-de-luce?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: I do not know dat.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: No; ’tis hereafter to know, but now to promise. Do but now promise,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Kate, you will endeavour for your French part of such a boy; and for my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: English moiety, take the word of a king and a bachelor. How answer you,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: _la plus belle Katherine du monde, mon très cher et divin déesse?_

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Your Majestee ’ave _fausse_ French enough to deceive de most _sage

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: demoiselle_ dat is _en France_.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now, fie upon my false French! By mine honour, in true English, I love

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: thee, Kate; by which honour I dare not swear thou lovest me; yet my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: blood begins to flatter me that thou dost, notwithstanding the poor and

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: untempering effect of my visage. Now, beshrew my father’s ambition! He

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: was thinking of civil wars when he got me; therefore was I created with

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: a stubborn outside, with an aspect of iron, that, when I come to woo

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ladies, I fright them. But, in faith, Kate, the elder I wax, the better

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I shall appear. My comfort is, that old age, that ill layer up of

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: beauty, can do no more spoil upon my face. Thou hast me, if thou hast

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: me, at the worst; and thou shalt wear me, if thou wear me, better and

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: better; and therefore tell me, most fair Katharine, will you have me?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Put off your maiden blushes; avouch the thoughts of your heart with the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: looks of an empress; take me by the hand, and say, Harry of England, I

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: am thine; which word thou shalt no sooner bless mine ear withal, but I

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: will tell thee aloud, England is thine, Ireland is thine, France is

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: thine, and Henry Plantagenet is thine; who, though I speak it before

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: his face, if he be not fellow with the best king, thou shalt find the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: best king of good fellows. Come, your answer in broken music; for thy

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: voice is music and thy English broken; therefore, queen of all,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Katharine, break thy mind to me in broken English. Wilt thou have me?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Dat is as it shall please _le roi mon père_.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Nay, it will please him well, Kate; it shall please him, Kate.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Den it sall also content me.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Upon that I kiss your hand, and call you my queen.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Laissez, mon seigneur, laissez, laissez! Ma foi, je ne veux point que

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: vous abaissiez votre grandeur en baisant la main d’une—Notre

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Seigneur!—indigne serviteur. Excusez-moi, je vous supplie, mon

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: très-puissant seigneur._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then I will kiss your lips, Kate.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: _Les dames et demoiselles pour être baisées devant leurs noces, il

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: n’est pas la coutume de France._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Madame my interpreter, what says she?

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: Dat it is not be de fashion _pour les_ ladies of France,—I cannot tell

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: wat is _baiser en_ Anglish.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To kiss.

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: Your Majestee _entend_ bettre _que moi_.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: It is not a fashion for the maids in France to kiss before they are

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: married, would she say?

lines.speaker: ALICE
lines.text: _Oui, vraiment._

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O Kate, nice customs curtsy to great kings. Dear Kate, you and I cannot

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: be confined within the weak list of a country’s fashion. We are the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: makers of manners, Kate; and the liberty that follows our places stops

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: the mouth of all find-faults, as I will do yours, for upholding the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: nice fashion of your country in denying me a kiss; therefore, patiently

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: and yielding. [_Kissing her._] You have witchcraft in your lips, Kate;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: there is more eloquence in a sugar touch of them than in the tongues of

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: the French council; and they should sooner persuade Harry of England

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: than a general petition of monarchs. Here comes your father.
Enter the French Power and the English Lords.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: God save your Majesty! My royal cousin, teach you our princess English?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I would have her learn, my fair cousin, how perfectly I love her; and

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: that is good English.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Is she not apt?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Our tongue is rough, coz, and my condition is not smooth; so that,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: having neither the voice nor the heart of flattery about me, I cannot

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: so conjure up the spirit of love in her, that he will appear in his

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: true likeness.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Pardon the frankness of my mirth, if I answer you for that. If you

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: would conjure in her, you must make a circle; if conjure up Love in her

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: in his true likeness, he must appear naked and blind. Can you blame her

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: then, being a maid yet ros’d over with the virgin crimson of modesty,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: if she deny the appearance of a naked blind boy in her naked seeing

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: self? It were, my lord, a hard condition for a maid to consign to.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet they do wink and yield, as love is blind and enforces.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: They are then excus’d, my lord, when they see not what they do.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then, good my lord, teach your cousin to consent winking.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: I will wink on her to consent, my lord, if you will teach her to know

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: my meaning; for maids, well summer’d and warm kept, are like flies at

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Bartholomew-tide, blind, though they have their eyes; and then they

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: will endure handling, which before would not abide looking on.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This moral ties me over to time and a hot summer; and so I shall catch

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: the fly, your cousin, in the latter end, and she must be blind too.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: As love is, my lord, before it loves.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: It is so; and you may, some of you, thank love for my blindness, who

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: cannot see many a fair French city for one fair French maid that stands

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: in my way.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Yes, my lord, you see them perspectively, the cities turn’d into a

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: maid; for they are all girdled with maiden walls that no war hath

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: entered.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Shall Kate be my wife?

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: So please you.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I am content, so the maiden cities you talk of may wait on her; so the

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: maid that stood in the way for my wish shall show me the way to my

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: will.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: We have consented to all terms of reason.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Is’t so, my lords of England?

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: The king hath granted every article;

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: His daughter first, and then in sequel all,

lines.speaker: WESTMORLAND
lines.text: According to their firm proposed natures.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Only he hath not yet subscribed this: where your Majesty demands, that

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: the King of France, having any occasion to write for matter of grant,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: shall name your Highness in this form and with this addition, in

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: French, _Notre très-cher fils Henri, Roi d’Angleterre, Héritier de

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: France_; and thus in Latin, _Praeclarissimus filius noster Henricus,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: rex Angliae et haeres Franciae._

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Nor this I have not, brother, so denied

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: But our request shall make me let it pass.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I pray you then, in love and dear alliance,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let that one article rank with the rest;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And thereupon give me your daughter.

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Take her, fair son, and from her blood raise up

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Issue to me; that the contending kingdoms

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Of France and England, whose very shores look pale

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: With envy of each other’s happiness,

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: May cease their hatred; and this dear conjunction

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: Plant neighbourhood and Christian-like accord

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: In their sweet bosoms, that never war advance

lines.speaker: FRENCH KING
lines.text: His bleeding sword ’twixt England and fair France.

lines.speaker: LORDS
lines.text: Amen!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Now, welcome, Kate; and bear me witness all,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That here I kiss her as my sovereign queen.
[_Flourish._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: God, the best maker of all marriages,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Combine your hearts in one, your realms in one!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: As man and wife, being two, are one in love,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: So be there ’twixt your kingdoms such a spousal,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: That never may ill office, or fell jealousy,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Which troubles oft the bed of blessed marriage,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Thrust in between the paction of these kingdoms,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: To make divorce of their incorporate league;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: That English may as French, French Englishmen,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ISABEL
lines.text: Receive each other. God speak this Amen!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Amen!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Prepare we for our marriage; on which day,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My Lord of Burgundy, we’ll take your oath,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And all the peers’, for surety of our leagues,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then shall I swear to Kate, and you to me;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And may our oaths well kept and prosperous be!
[_Sennet. Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: Enter Chorus.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Thus far, with rough and all-unable pen,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Our bending author hath pursu’d the story,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: In little room confining mighty men,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Mangling by starts the full course of their glory.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Small time, but in that small most greatly lived

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: This star of England. Fortune made his sword,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: By which the world’s best garden he achieved,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: And of it left his son imperial lord.

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Henry the Sixth, in infant bands crown’d King

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Of France and England, did this king succeed;

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Whose state so many had the managing,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: That they lost France and made his England bleed:

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: Which oft our stage hath shown; and, for their sake,

lines.speaker: CHORUS
lines.text: In your fair minds let this acceptance take.
[_Exit._]
